articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce's $30 million 1587 Prime offers $102 Thanksgiving dinner amid ongoing legal dispute
articles.summary: Thanksgiving is getting a luxury twist in Kansas City, thanks to Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce.
articles.body: Thanksgiving is getting a luxury twist in Kansas City, thanks to Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce. The two Kansas City Chiefs teammates are bringing holiday favourites to the table at their upscale steakhouse, 1587 Prime. But this is no ordinary Thanksgiving dinner. From an $80 prime rib to lobster bisque and pumpkin cake, the restaurant has put together a menu that could make the holiday meal feel like a special occasion. Diners can enjoy a premium combination for just over $100, although traditional options are also available.Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce reveal their $102 Thanksgiving menu at 1587 PrimeThe Thanksgiving celebration at 1587 Prime is scheduled for November 26, 2026, with the restaurant welcoming guests between 2 p.m. and 8 p.m. The special menu brings together classic holiday food and high-end steakhouse dishes, giving Kansas City diners several ways to celebrate.The standout option is a 16-ounce prime rib, priced at $80. Those who prefer seafood can start with lobster bisque for $22. Ordering both would bring the bill to $102 before taxes and gratuity.However, guests looking for a more traditional Thanksgiving plate have another choice. The restaurant is offering stuffed turkey roulade for $55 per person. Other additions include pumpkin cake for $18 and a seasonal Gather & Give cocktail for $19.This means diners do not have to commit to one fixed holiday package. They can select individual dishes based on their appetite and budget. A turkey roulade with pumpkin cake, for instance, would cost $73 before additional charges.The restaurant has become another business venture connecting the two Chiefs stars outside football. Its name, 1587 Prime, combines Mahomes' jersey number 15 with Kelce's number 87.Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce face trademark dispute over 1587 PrimeWhile the Thanksgiving menu is attracting attention, the restaurant is also dealing with a legal challenge over its name.1587 Sneakers, a footwear and apparel company, filed a federal trademark infringement lawsuit in February 2026. The company claims that the steakhouse's name and related merchandise could confuse customers familiar with its existing brand.Mahomes, Kelce and their hospitality partner, Noble 33, are among the defendants named in the case.The players' legal representatives have sought to dismiss the claims against them, arguing that their involvement does not provide sufficient grounds for personal liability. However, 1587 Sneakers has pushed back, describing the two NFL stars as the "moving forces" behind the restaurant's identity.The dispute remains unresolved, and no finding of trademark infringement has been established.For now, the legal battle has not stopped the restaurant from welcoming customers or preparing its Thanksgiving service. For Mahomes and Kelce, the holiday menu offers another chance to bring their business venture into the spotlight, this time away from the football field.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "Absurd, Ridiculous, Poisonous Spin": Megyn Kelly has a harsh message for Dianna Russini after her comeback interview sparks fresh questions about the scandal
articles.summary: Dianna Russini’s planned return to sports media has drawn a sharp response from Megyn Kelly, who believes a recent People profile focused too much on
articles.body: Dianna Russini’s planned return to sports media has drawn a sharp response from Megyn Kelly, who believes a recent People profile focused too much on personal recovery and too little on professional accountability. Russini discussed the effect the controversy had on her family and her hopes of becoming an example for women rebuilding their careers. Kelly, speaking with journalist Matt Taibbi, rejected that framing and questioned why the interview did not press Russini harder about the circumstances that led to her departure from The Athletic. Russini is due back with a new NFL show on November 11.Megyn Kelly challenges the comeback narrativeKelly’s criticism targeted both Russini and the way People presented her story. After reading passages from the interview, the former Fox News host called it “absurd, ridiculous, poisonous spin that takes zero responsibility for what she actually did”.Russini had spoken about how the controversy reached her grandmother, cousins and other relatives. She said the experience changed how she viewed the people touched by her reporting. She also said she hoped to show other women that a difficult period does not have to end a career.“I really hope I can be someone other women see. You can pick yourself up, get back out there, and not be afraid,” Russini said.Kelly was not persuaded. Speaking with Taibbi, she questioned the interview’s emphasis on resilience while leaving, in her view, important questions about Russini’s professional judgment unanswered.That is the central divide. Russini’s account focused on the personal cost of the episode and the challenge of returning to work. Kelly argued that a comeback profile should also examine the decisions that made the comeback necessary, particularly the boundaries journalists must maintain with people they cover.Russini’s new NFL show begins November 11Russini’s return is no longer just an ambition. BetUS announced that “The Russini Report,” a weekly live show accompanied by a column, will premiere Nov. 11. It gives her a direct route back into NFL coverage, where she built her career.The controversy dates to April, when photographs showed Russini and New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel together at an Arizona resort. Both initially denied that their relationship was romantic. Russini later resigned from The Athletic.The publication’s investigation found that Russini should have disclosed the nature of the relationship so editors could assess her assignments. It did not determine whether the relationship was romantic. That distinction matters: the finding about disclosure is not proof of a romantic relationship.In her People interview, Russini referred to support from people around the NFL and said the experience would shape her approach to future stories. Her new programme will give audiences a chance to judge her work again, but the questions surrounding her exit remain.Kelly’s response underlines the challenge facing Russini. Returning to football coverage may restore a familiar routine, but it does not settle the debate over disclosure, judgment and trust. Those questions could follow her into the new show.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

The massive mansion features eight bedrooms and nine-and-a-half bathrooms.With over 13,000 sq.ft. of sleek, ultra-luxurious living space, the property perfectly suits one of the league’s elite signal-callers and high-performance lifestyle. However, it looks like the 2026 season has not been one of his best, as he is currently down with zero wins and eight losses. Anyhow, coming back to his real estate portfolio.The 28-year-old quarterback purchased a $5.25 million Southern California estate in 2022, according to Ramon Weber of Mansions Radar. The property is known for its high purchase price and exclusive, highly private location.Justin Herbert’s Southern California homeJustin Herbert’s 5,000 sq ft home sits close to the coast and near the Los Angeles Chargers’ practice and training facilities. The neighborhood type is a private residential pocket, tucked away from main roads to offer maximum privacy. It takes about 20 minutes by car to reach SoFi Stadium.The property is situated along the Southern California coast, in the Orange County/Los Angeles area. From the outside, its dark trim, pale stucco, and big windows catch the coastal light.There is no sign, house number, or inclination that a Los Angeles Chargers quarterback lives there, according to Mansions Radar’s Ramon Weber. A walkway leads to the entrance. The main living room sits at the center of the floor plan, with the kitchen on one side and the backyard on the other.The living room features a light color palette and simple furniture. The Southern California home also includes an exclusive training setup, or the home gym, where the quarterback can work out in complete privacy, away from the constant attention of paparazzi.Justin Herbert’s game room and private luxury resortThere’s an additional space for a game room, complete with framed artwork, display shelves, a television, a pool table, and a fully equipped bar. It acts as the perfect space suitable for hosting friends and family.It gives Justin Herbert all the relaxation he needs. At the moment, he needs it more than ever - given the stress, criticism, and fan frustration surrounding the Los Angeles Chargers’ 0-8 record in the 2026 season.The primary bedroom boasts large windows that bring in natural light. Soft beiges and warm browns give the spacious layout a comfortable, homely feel.On the outside, there is a swimming pool surrounded by poolside loungers, plush-cream-colored sofas and armchairs. A small, covered pavilion features comfortable seating, providing a shaded retreat. The outdoor space feels like a private luxury resort in itself.Justin Herbert’s alleged estate with Madison BeerMadison Beer News wrote on X that Madison Beer and Justin Herbert were in the process of buying a $20 million mansion together. The source was cited as “Deuxmoi.”However, these claims were merely rumors and were not verified. Athlon Sports’ Rodney Knuppel later reported that there was no official report that Herbert and Beer were buying a mansion.“No legal filings, no real estate listings, and no credible news outlet has confirmed the story,” Athlon Sports’ Rodney Knuppel wrote. “It appears to be a case of social media assuming the next chapter based on how visible the pair has been this fall. Fact-checking confirms that the story is unverified, and fans should treat it as just that. A rumor.”The property mentioned by House of Celebs as Herbert’s real estate is reportedly worth $18 million. And Madison Beer News claims that Herbert and Beer were buying a $20 million house together in Los Angeles. Are both claims talking about the same property? Or are we as confused as ever?As things stand, there is no verified evidence establishing that Herbert owns an $18 million Los Angeles estate. articles.title: NFL midseason awards: The good, the bad and the Dallas Cowboys
articles.summary: We're handing out high-school-style awards to all 32 NFL teams at the halfway point. Some will be proud. Others should probably skip the reunion.
articles.body:
We're at the turn of the 2026 NFL season, and it's time to recognize the best (and not-so-best) players, teams and moments of the year to date. We're doing this high-school-yearbook style, and we're also doing this equitably — everyone gets an award, but everyone doesn't get a good award, because not everyone deserves a good reward. (Howdy, Dallas.) And now, without further ado, the NFL Superlatives at the 2026 halfway (-ish) mark:

Everybody loves Buffalo. Everybody's very impressed by Buffalo. Everybody's thinking Buffalo is headed to the Super Bowl. And everybody might be right! Just don't think about how many popular kids peaked in high school … or, in this case, the regular season.

They announced their intentions with a 59-point eruption to start the season, and the Bears are still on track for a landmark year. Every element of this team was in place from the jump or upgraded via trade. Caution: Bears ahead.

Need a good laugh? Watch Dallas' defense try to contain an opponent in the final minutes of a game! You'll never see anything quite so hapless and ridiculous in your life! (Not recommended for children or Dallas fans.)

Cutest Couple: Joe Burrow & Ja'Marr Chase, Cincinnati Bengals

Already the source of one of the NFL's great quotes of the 2020s — "F*** it, Ja'Marr's down there somewhere" — Burrow & Chase are doing what they've done since their LSU days, and the rest of the league, starting with Buffalo, is eyeing them warily.

The Jags are the nerd who spent the summer working out, getting contacts and learning a few dance moves. And now that they've shocked people with their good looks and they're stealing lunch money (star players) from other nerds (the NFC South). This is one hell of a star-making arc they're on.

Most Athletic: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Seattle Seahawks

The rest of the Super Bowl champion Seahawks may have regressed to the mean or to the blue medical tent, but Smith-Njigba is out there tearing it up solo, with more receiving yards (1,036) and touchdowns (9) than any other receivers in the game.

Remember what we said about everybody getting an award? Yeah. Anyway, the Commanders' burgundy unis harken back to the glory days of the franchise, when Washington was a Super Bowl champion, a perpetual contender, and one of the league's must-watch teams. As opposed to now, when they are … not.

Most Thoughtful: Jordan Love, Green Bay Packers

Love is in the air, baby! Jordan's 2,618 passing yards lead the NFL, and he's generous with his touchdowns, distributing seven to Christian Watson and five to Matthew Golden already. All you need is Love … and maybe a couple decent receivers, too.

This is a two-way award. The Vikings are the most defense-minded team in the league, and they've racked up six wins and a likely playoff berth that way. But they're also defensive as in touchy, like when you mention that mayyyybe they shouldn't have cut ties with a quarterback who went on to win the Super Bowl, or with a top-10 draft pick who's now doing just fine in New York, or that they're going backward (Kirk Cousins) to go forward. Defense wins championships, defensiveness doesn't.

Most Offensive (complimentary): San Francisco 49ers

Just reliably winning game after game, scoring more touchdowns than any team in the NFL (31 to date) and controlling the mighty NFC West. If it turns out that electrical substation has been giving the 49ers super-powers, everyone's going to want one.

Most Offensive (not complimentary): Los Angeles Chargers

If ever a football team should be rated NC-17, it's this one. Subjecting international audiences to the Chargers may in fact violate the Geneva Convention. May cause uncontrollable vomiting. Watch only under a doctor's care.

Best way to protect your fragile quarterback? Don't let him throw a pass. At all. The Bucs and Baker Mayfield got weird against the Falcons in a rainstorm a couple weeks back, and somehow managed to win a key divisional game without completing a single pass. (Points off for the game being against the Falcons, who could find a way to lose a football game against a baseball team.) Todd Bowles' seat has gone from "nuclear" to "pleasantly warm on a winter's morning."

The 'He Can't Keep Getting Away With This' Award: Sean Payton and the Denver Broncos

Somehow, Denver has won 16 straight one-possession games, a remarkable testament to the Broncos' resilience, defensive rigidity and offensive adequacy. The Week 8 victory against Kansas City with the Chiefs on Denver's goal line will stand as the most notable of the season until they can get one in February.

No, not Sir Purr, though he's cool. Mascot of the year is now Lennox, the corgi who got loose during a halftime show and piled up an impressive rushing total:

Great run with multiple broken tackles, but you've got to take it to the house, Lennox! End zone was right there!

Most Likely To Go Broke In Vegas: Detroit Lions

You can spot the signs of a shaky gambler a mile away: splitting 10s, doubling after every loss, going for it on fourth down in your own territory. The Lions and Dan Campbell have survived so far, but the odds are coming for Detroit, one way or another. (No, Detroit doesn't play Las Vegas this year. It was a metaphor.)

Some weeks, the Falcons look like absolute playoff contenders, fearsome on the ground and lethal through the air. And some weeks, they look like they've started the other team's defense in their fantasy lineup. Is Michael Penix Jr. a strong quarterback with bad spurts, or a terrible quarterback with flashes of genius? The answer, of course, is yes. And also no.

The Seventh Year Seniors: Kansas City Chiefs

Did you ever look around a party back in high school and see somebody who was definitely too old to still be hanging around there? Yeah, that's Kansas City. The quarterback is still cruising on the glories of his youth, the tight end went off and got married, and the head coach's mustache continues to expand every year. Sure, there's a new running back in town making everyone feel young again, but you have to wonder … how much longer are they all going to keep doing this?

Most Likely to Lose Their Security Deposit: Tennessee Titans

When you're weeks from moving out of your old place, you don't really much care if it gets trashed. That's the Titans right now, just a few months away from moving into swanky new digs next door. So yeah, if you go to Old Nissan Stadium, go ahead, put a hole in the wall, throw some furniture out the window, burn your name into the turf. It's all getting knocked down soon enough anyway. Nothing matters, especially not the standings.

Most Likely To Host a Party When Parents Are Out of Town: New Orleans Saints

Look, if you can't be the most popular or most athletic kid in class, at least make sure you can offer a cool place for everybody to hang out.

There's nothing worse than being tagged with "potential," unless it's being tabbed as "preseason Super Bowl pick." The Rams sleepwalked — almost literally — through their opening game against San Francisco in Australia, and haven't woken up since. Maybe the return of Myles Garrett can scare them out of their slumber?

Best Hang: Arizona Cardinals and Gardner Minshew

There was always one long-haired dude hanging around school — maybe he was a student, maybe he wasn't — and everybody sort of gave him a wide berth. But when you get to know him, you're surprised at how sharp and funny he is — and how he can jump up from lunch and guide your team to a win over the Dallas Cowboys, too.

The 'One Year Away From Being One Year Away' Award: New York Jets

Did you know that the Jets (as the standings now sit) have two of the first six picks, and three of the first 13, in next year's NFL draft? It's true: they have their own, plus picks belonging to the Colts and Cowboys. How will the Jets manage to screw this up? Let's watch and see!

The 'Losing Texas' Award: Houston Texans

Houston went Full Minnesota — going all-in on defense and hoping the quarterback was competent enough to win games 10-7 and 7-3 — and, well, it hasn't worked out yet. Two of their three wins have come against teams with a combined 1-15 record. The third came against division leader Jacksonville, so maybe there's a scrap of hope.

Most Likely to Run for President: Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers

Rodgers is doing a little low-key image rehab this year in Pittsburgh, methodically guiding the Steelers to a 6-2 record and a share of the AFC North lead. Rodgers says this is his last year in uniform, and we believe him, but will he remain silent in retirement? We're just asking questions.

Most Visits to the School Clinic: Philadelphia Eagles

The City of Brotherly Deductibles has had a rough 2026. You could make a pretty good starting lineup of Eagles players who have missed games this season (Jalen Hurts, Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert, Nolan Smith…). With a bevy of draft picks in the years ahead, Philadelphia is just going to lie down until this feeling goes away.

Most Likely to Change The Subject: New England Patriots

So much not to talk about in New England these days! Is this quarterback the second coming of You Know Who, or just a lucky journeyman? Did the Pats get fat and happy on a soft schedule last year? And what exactly is the head coach's new media policy? Next question.

The 'What Goes Up Always Comes Down' Award: Cleveland Browns

Admit it. You were a little unsettled when the Browns were 5-2 and leading the AFC North. Since then, they've lost two straight and are looking like the Browns we know so well. Order has been restored in the universe.

Boy, the Giants were feeling fine after their Week 1 win over Dallas. And just as quickly, hopes deflated when Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending injury in Week 2. But somehow, the Giants have cobbled together win after win, using quarterback after quarterback, and suddenly they're dangerous. Granted, it's a "is that stray dog going to beg for food or bite my face?" kind of dangerous, but it's better than nothing.

The 'I Will Remember You' Award: Baltimore Ravens

Everything was set up so well for Baltimore this season — new head coach, new offensive coordinator, new sense of joy and hope in the organization. And then Lamar Jackson suffered an ankle sprain in Week 4, followed by a thumb injury on the very first play of his return in Week 8, and the good vibes would return nevermore.

Like the fabled Grand Theft Auto VI video game, the Miami Dolphins play in the neon-and-vice world of South Florida. Like GTAVI, the more you immerse yourself in the Dolphins, the more your moral center slips away. And like GTAVI, we've been waiting for the Dolphins to show up for so, so many years.

The 'Lighting Matches in a Fireworks Factory' Award: Indianapolis Colts

Ah, the AFC South, where a 2-7 record is good enough to be just a game out of second place. The Colts are headed for one of those surgical scourings, and everybody not named Irsay or Jonathan Taylor is at risk. At least they'll have a high first-round pick … which they've already sent to the Jets. Whoops.

Most Cheerful: Fernando Mendoza and the Las Vegas Raiders

Mendoza was a charismatic revelation last season as he led Indiana to a national championship and won the Heisman along the way. Drafted by Las Vegas, he spent the first half of the season behind Kirk Cousins … right up until Cousins was traded to Minnesota. Friendly Fernando thus gets his first NFL start against … the Super Bowl champion Seahawks. Let's just see how long he keeps smiling through all that. Raiders fans just have to hope this isn't the real-world version of the "I'm in Danger" meme .

articles.title: Might Fernando Mendoza actually be in ideal situation with the Raiders?
articles.summary: NFL analyst Danny Parkins believes Fernando Mendoza is in a good situation with Las Vegas Raiders after trading Kirk Cousins to Minnesota.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders went through a seismic change at quarterback midway through the 2026 NFL season. They have cleared the way for top overall pick Fernando Mendoza to lead the offense after trading Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a 2027 third-round pick.

Some NFL analysts are skeptical about Mendoza's performances against the Raiders next two opponents. After all, the Seattle Seahawks and the Denver Broncos have some of the best defensive units this season.

But one NFL analyst is not worried about the situation that Mendoza will be facing.

"He is going into a good situation," said Fox analyst Danny Parkins on First Things First. "I think (Klint) Kubiak is a good coach. We've seen that now year over year. It's not a bad situation that he is walking into."

Before the Raiders' Week 10 game against the Seahawks, Mendoza has had one regular season appearance. He completed six throws out of eight attempts for 48 yards during their Week 5 loss to the New England Patriots.

Parkins knows that the situation could turn ugly for the former Indiana standout against Seattle. However, he mentioned that struggling offenses have been a recurring theme against the Seahawks this season.

With eight games left and the playoff hunt still active, Parkins believes that the 2025 Heisman Trophy winner will do good as the Raiders' starter.

"I think Mendoza is going to be fine. It's a huge coup for the Raiders that they can get a top 100 pick for a guy who's not gonna be there in the future," Parkins added.

Mendoza will now lead an offense that ranks eighth in points (26.4) and fifth in passing yards (259.7) per game.

articles.title: NFL legend eying Troy Aikman's 'Monday Night Football' seat
articles.summary: Aikman and Joe Buck appear to be heading toward a divorce
articles.body:
Troy Aikman's frustration with ESPN and longtime broadcast partner Joe Buck has been anything but a secret, as the former Dallas Cowboys star is looking increasingly checked out with his contract expiring in February.

What remains unknown is who'll replace Aikman as ESPN's Monday Night Football analyst. Well, another NFL legend just threw his hat in the ring.

Drew Brees, the former New Orleans Saints star who's currently an analyst for Fox, is eying Aikman's MNF seat, according to Front Office Sports . Whether he lands the ESPN job is uncertain, but a No. 1 game analyst role is Brees' goal.

"That's my goal and aspiration, and that's what I'm working towards," Brees said . "Every week, I feel like it's getting better and better and more comfortable."

Brees has rebounded as a media presence after a much-maligned one-year stint with NBC in 2021. Still, he faces plenty of competition for the MNF seat from the likes of Greg Olsen and Tony Romo.

Aikman, who's upset over how ESPN and the recently extended Buck handled contract negotiations, is signed through the Super Bowl in February.

articles.title: Keenan Allen Traded to 49ers From Colts at NFL Deadline, Updated Depth Chart, Salary Cap
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts traded wide receiver Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers for a 2027 sixth-round draft pick.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts traded wide receiver Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers for a 2027 sixth-round draft pick.

The team also signed cornerback Jack Jones to its practice squad on Wednesday.

Allen offers immediate help to a 49ers' wide receiver room that has unfortunately been hit hard with injuries.

Here's a preview of what the 49ers' updated depth chart could look like after the Allen trade, alongside what's listed via Ourlads .

WR (Z and Slot): Deebo Samuel Sr., Keenan Allen, De'Zhaun Stribling, Jordan Watkins

The 49ers were listed as having $35.2 million in cap space before the trade, per Over the Cap . Allen signed a one-year, $3.3 million contract with the Colts last offseason. In sum, San Francisco has plenty of cap room to add Allen, and it might be a bargain all things considered.

The 34-year-old Allen has played 14 NFL seasons for the San Diego/Los Angeles Chargers, Chicago Bears and Indianapolis Colts. He's a six-time Pro Bowler with five 100-reception campaigns and five 1,000-yard seasons.

In eight games with the Colts, Allen caught 40 passes for 351 yards and one touchdown.

Now he joins a 49ers team that is very much in position to make a Super Bowl run. Allen provides a much-needed reinforcement in the wideout room.

San Francisco got this deal done just in time prior to the 4 p.m. trade deadline on Tuesday. One can presume Allen should be in line to make his San Francisco debut on Sunday at the Dallas Cowboys.

Former Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike Tomlin isn't yet focused on a return to the sidelines as he continues his broadcast work for NBC Sports.

Tomlin told reporters Wednesday he hasn't "given one iota of thought about coaching." However, he didn't totally rule out the idea.

Front Office Sports' Mark Maske reported in October that Tomlin is likely to be targeted by NFL teams this offseason, "but it's not considered automatic that he would leave his broadcasting job."

The 54-year-old isn't old in coaching terms. Working 19 seasons in the job is a long time, though, and this is the first time in two decades he has taken a step back to reset.

Tomlin has generally received positive reviews for his work with NBC. He might be enjoying the work more than he expected.

Fans have also discovered his passions extend well beyond football. It was mesmerizing to watch Tomlin earnestly describe the thought and effort he put into building his own city in Minecraft.

There's no question the interest from NFL teams will be there.

Tomlin has a .628 career winning percentage, and leaving Pittsburgh could be exactly what he needed because his tenure had run its course. There's no reason to think he has suffered from taking a season off, either, after both Sean Payton and Mike Vrabel thrived in their new settings after a gap year.

Whether Tomlin is eager to jump back into a coaching job is another matter. He's being well compensated by NBC and working far less than he had before.

articles.title: Bengals' Message to Eagles After Scrapped Arnold Ebiketie Trade Revealed by HC Zac Taylor
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor addressed the situation around the aborted Arnold Ebiketie trade with the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor addressed the situation around the aborted Arnold Ebiketie trade with the Philadelphia Eagles.

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Taylor explained on behalf of Bengals de facto general manager Duke Tobin that the decision to cancel the deal was on their end and the Eagles were "a great trade partner."

When asked about specifics of what led to the decision, Taylor said he never asked the front office and it only took up "about three minutes" of his day.

The Bengals initially agreed to send a 2027 sixth-round draft pick to Philadelphia for Ebiketie to boost their defensive line depth.

A short time after the deal was agreed upon, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported the Bengals decided to call off the deal.

Cincinnati's decision came after Nick Korte of Over the Cap posted on X that the trade would actually end up taking away a third-round compensatory pick in the 2027 draft the Bengals would receive for losing Trey Hendrickson in free agency last offseason on top of the sixth-rounder they were going to give up.

Per Albert Breer of The MMQB, the NFL put a rule in place to prevent teams from exploiting a loophole involving sign-and-trade deals by making it so a player moved in the first year of his contract counts against the compensatory pick formula as if the acquiring team signed him.

Ebiketie signed a one-year, $7.3 million contract with the Eagles in March after playing the first four years of his NFL career with the Atlanta Falcons.

The 27-year-old Ebiketie has appeared in each of Philadelphia's nine games so far this season. He has 25 combined tackles, two quarterback hits and no sacks.

In the wake of the Ebiketie situation, the Bengals ultimately made no moves before the trade deadline passed at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday. They are currently in first place in the AFC North with a 6-2 record, having won four straight games.

Cincinnati will look to extend its winning streak to five games on Sunday Night Football against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

articles.title: Matt LaFleur 'Shocked' by Kirk Cousins Trade Price After Vikings-Raiders Deal at NFL Deadline
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur was "shocked" that the Minnesota Vikings only had to give up a 2027 third-round draft pick to the Las Vegas Raiders for quarterback Kirk Cousins.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur was "shocked" that the Minnesota Vikings only had to give up a 2027 third-round draft pick to the Las Vegas Raiders for quarterback Kirk Cousins.

"I was surprised they didn't get more for him, quite honestly. I was shocked when I saw what they traded him for. It was mind-blowing to me," LaFleur told reporters at his press conference on Wednesday.

LaFleur's Packers will host Cousins' Vikings on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET in a crucial NFC North showdown.

Report: Raiders Gave Cousins Trade Choice

LaFleur has no doubt that Cousins will be QB1 on Sunday.

"Yeah, he'll be out there. He'll be starting. I'm fairly confident of that. Obviously he's got familiarity with their system. Even if he didn't, he's a really intelligent guy, and I think he's been playing at a high level."

Cousins played for the Vikings from 2018-2023. His final two seasons in town were under current head coach (and offensive play-caller) Kevin O'Connell, so Cousins has a strong familiarity with his system. In other words, the transition shouldn't be too difficult on paper.

Cousins also did quite well under O'Connell, completing 67.1 percent of his passes for 6,878 yards (7.2 yards per attempt), 49 touchdowns and 19 interceptions in 25 games. Unfortunately, a torn Achilles cut Cousins' 2023 season short after eight games.

The 15-year veteran is still slinging it at age 38, completing 64.1 percent of his passes for 2,340 yards (7.4 yards per attempt), 20 touchdowns (second in the league) and eight interceptions in nine games for the Raiders. His passing yards places him fifth overall.

The 6-2 Vikings are 27th in scoring but No. 1 in scoring defense. Kicker Will Reichard, the reigning First Team All-Pro, is one of the NFL's best at his position (if not the best). They needed a quarterback to jumpstart this offense, as this team looks like a Super Bowl contender if that can happen.

Enter Cousins, who arrives just in time for a massive matchup with the 6-3 Packers amid a NFC North where the 7-2 Chicago Bears and 6-2 Detroit Lions are also battling for the division crown.

articles.title: Josh Downs 'Screamed' After Trade to Chiefs from Colts, WR's Jersey Number Revealed
articles.summary: After being sent from the Indianapolis Colts to the Kansas City Chiefs at Tuesday's trade deadline, wide receiver Josh Downs is hyped about his new home.
articles.body:
After being sent from the Indianapolis Colts to the Kansas City Chiefs at Tuesday's trade deadline, wide receiver Josh Downs is hyped about his new home.

"It's great to join a team like this. It's good when guys welcome you. … I don't want to be a guy who ask what the play is and the formation. I was excited for the opportunity. I kind of screamed when I saw the text," Downs told reporters on Wednesday.

Downs, who wore No. 2 with the Colts, also told reporters that he will be wearing No. 12 going forward.

After the Colts traded Downs to the Chiefs on Tuesday in exchange for 2027 fourth-and fifth-round picks, the 25-year-old immediately let his excitement be known by posting a Vince Carter GIF on social media. He followed up with a thank-you message to the Colts, who had drafted him with a third-round pick in 2023.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported last month that Downs had requested to be traded from Indianapolis amid the team's disappointing year. He's now joining a Kansas City team that is in the thick of the playoff hunt in the AFC with a 6-2 record.

In nine games this season, Downs has recorded 33 catches for 354 yards and a touchdown. Those numbers would make him the Chiefs' second-leading receiver behind only tight end Travis Kelce. He should quickly become one of the top targets for Kansas City star quarterback Patrick Mahomes.

"From meeting Josh today, the mindset he has, he's going to help us," Mahomes told reporters on Wednesday. "... You can tell the intellect and he's a professional and he wants to win."

Downs will get the first chance to show his skills when the Chiefs face the Atlanta Falcons (3-6) on Sunday.

articles.title: Titans' Calvin Ridley: 'I took my keys' from airport valet, who 'yelled I broke his finger;' doesn't know if he'll face charges
articles.summary: Per a report, an airport valet wants to press charges against Ridley following a dispute that escalated when the valet wouldn't give Ridley the keys to his t...
articles.body:
For the first time since the Tennessee Titans acknowledged that Calvin Ridley was involved in an "incident" at the Nashville airport, the wide receiver told his side of the story Wednesday.

Per Ridley, he was involved in a back-and-forth with an airport valet as he attempted to recover the keys to his truck. Ridley spoke about the incident with reporters at his locker.

Ridley said he took his truck keys from the valet's hands when he didn't have a ticket to retrieve them and that the valet said he sustained an injury to one of his fingers. He said he did so after showing the valet multiple documents to verify the truck was his.

"I took my keys out of his hand," Ridley said. "I didn't have the ticket. Once you don't have the ticket, you show him your ID, you fill out a form. I also showed him a picture, I also showed him more that it's my truck.

"My wife and kids was at the top. My mom was at the top. I came down by myself to get it. It's 11 p.m. at night. They gave me the hardest time to get my truck. I just got my keys, got the registration.

"They wanted the registration. I gave them the registration after I got the keys. My wife came down. We got in the truck and left."

Ridley: Valet 'yelled I broke his finger'

Ridley was asked if the the valet's hand got cut during the incident amid reports.

"I don't know what I did. I didn't look at nothing," Ridley answered. "He yelled I broke his finger. I don't know what happened."

Ridley said law enforcement hasn't reached out to him, and he doesn't know if he'll face charges from the incident. He said he was not detained at the airport.

Per an A to Z Sports report from Monday, the incident took place at the Nashville Airport on Saturday. Ridley's account lines up with some of the details of the report.

Report states the valet wanted to press charges

Citing sources, the report stated that Ridley grew frustrated when the airport valet wouldn't give him his truck keys. Ridley didn't have his ticket, and the valet couldn't verify the truck was Ridley's, per the report.

Ridley then grabbed his keys from the valet's hand, "and one of the keys (or something on the keychain) cut the valet's hand in the process," according to the report.

At that point, per the report, airport and TSA law enforcement were called to the scene, and the valet sought to press charges. It's not clear as of Wednesday if Ridley will face charges or any sort of discipline for the incident.

The Titans issued a statement on Sunday that they were "aware of the incident" and had been in contact with airport authorities. They did not offer details beyond that.

Head coach Robert Saleh also addressed the incident at his new conference Monday while declining to discuss details.

"From my understanding it was a very minor miscommunication at the airport," Saleh said . "Unfortunately, law enforcement has it, and that's about as far as I can go with commenting."

The incident took place days before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline. A former All-Pro, Ridley has played a reduced role with the Titans this season at 31 years old. He has six catches for 91 yards in seven appearances this season and was believed to be on the trade block ahead of Tuesday's deadline.

Ridley did not get traded and remains with the Titans.

articles.title: Giants reportedly called Falcons about RB Bijan Robinson ahead of trade deadline
articles.summary: In the first year of the John Harbaugh era, New York has been looking for more production from the running back position.
articles.body:
The New York Giants didn't make a trade-deadline splash, but that doesn't mean they didn't try to make waves.

In their latest attempt to upgrade their running back room, they made a call for Atlanta Falcons star Bijan Robinson, according to a Wednesday report from ESPN's Jordan Raanan.

It's unclear if the Giants actually made an offer for Robinson, per ESPN, which noted that the 24-year-old back is seen around the league as a player the Falcons value too much to move. He's a two-time Pro Bowler and currently leads the NFL with 880 rushing yards this season.

Early in the John Harbaugh era, New York has actively searched for a big-name back. The Giants, according to ESPN, inquired about reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III in free agency. Plus, they were reportedly interested in drafting Jeremiyah Love, who went No. 3 overall. And, per ESPN's report, New York made a trade offer to the Indianapolis Colts for Jonathan Taylor that was eventually taken off the table.

The Giants also reportedly contacted the Tennessee Titans about Tony Pollard.

As aggressive as the Giants have been under Harbaugh — he even called Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk directly in attempt to trade for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons — they drew a line when it came to the deadline.

"For most of these deals, they weren't going to overextend," Raanan said Tuesday on the "Giants Nation Show ."

"And a big part of that is they're not flush with picks right now."

Right before the deadline, Harbaugh was asked about his desire to add a playmaker.

"I'd be excited ... [for] the right guy," he said, via SNY . "My excitement level would be based on who the player is. You get the right player, then you're really excited. I wouldn't be excited for the not-right player. There's players you love and players you like. I would want a player that we love."

As for Robinson, he's in the upper echelon of active NFL running backs. Only Jahmyr Gibbs of the Detroit Lions has logged more scrimmage yards (1,132) than Robinson (1,130) this season.

At the moment, the Giants rank 17th in the league with 112.1 rushing yards per game. Of the team's four running backs who have carried the ball at least 19 times this season, the only one who's averaging at least 4 yards a pop is Cam Skattebo (4.3 yards per rush).

Skattebo leads New York with 418 yards and two touchdowns on the ground; however, he's fumbled four times — his mostly costly giveaway resulted in what was effectively a temporary benching — and he missed last week's road win over the Philadelphia Eagles because of a hamstring injury.

Right now, he's competing alongside fellow backs Devin Singletary and Greg Desrosiers Jr. Tyrone Tracy Jr. is on injured reserve, although his hamstring injury isn't considered season-ending.

While the 5-2-1 Giants browsed for backfield help, Skattebo will remain their lead back for now. He's expected to return for New York's Thursday night game versus the Washington Commanders.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins' Status for Vikings vs. Packers Discussed by HC After Raiders Trade at NFL Deadline
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley hinted Kirk Cousins could potentially jump right into the starting lineup beginning with Sunday's matchup at the Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley hinted Kirk Cousins could potentially jump right into the starting lineup beginning with Sunday's matchup at the Green Bay Packers.

Teasley told reporters Wednesday it would ultimately be up to head coach Kevin O'Connell to decide which quarterback will start.

"I would leave that to Kevin, he's going to put us in the best position to succeed," Teasley said. "But we also didn't acquire Kirk to not play."

Report: Raiders Gave Cousins Trade Choice

Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said as of Wednesday Kyler Murray is still week-to-week with a hamstring injury, but stopped short of naming Cousins starter against the Packers.

"I think it's still too early to commit wholeheartedly to what the plan on Sunday looks like, but I will say, excited about the opportunity of spending every moment we can between now and then to get [Cousins] comfortable and allow him to play for us this Sunday," O'Connell said.

"So, that's what we're working towards, but also want to be fair to Kirk and make sure he feels good about it."

Murray was sidelined with a Grade 2 hamstring strain from Monday's loss to the Buffalo Bills, during which Carson Wentz struggled as his replacement. The Vikings acquired Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders the following day.

"Kyler, he wasn't able to play on Monday," Teasley said. "I don't want to get into next week, but that's really what his status is... We're looking to acquire a player that's healthy, and able, and ready to go."

Teasley added he considered Cousins' existing familiarity with the Vikings and O'Connell's system as a "bonus."

When asked if Murray would get a chance to compete with Cousins for the QB1 job when healthy, O'Connell said he didn't "think you can have a competition during the season."

"We acquired Kirk to join a 6-2 football team and play, and as I told Kyler Murray... we really learned that 11 snaps into the season it was less than ideal, and then obviously having the hamstring set him back from maybe continuously stacking the momentum that he was building," O'Connell said.

"The way I look at it is, when Kyler's healthy, we'll have a quarterback room that obviously with Kirk, and hopefully his comfort and continuing to play as well as he has this year in our offense right now. We feel really good about that, but also feel really good about the potential to have Kyler Murray, Carson and Max [Brosmer] in that room."

O'Connell added Wentz, who went 6-for-23 and threw two interceptions in Monday's loss to the Bills, is limited with an ankle injury.

Should Wentz remain sidelined this weekend, the Vikings could be hoping to start Cousins with Brosmer as his backup.

Cousins, who most recently saw action Sunday with the Raiders, had started nine games prior to his trade and is now joining a Vikings team that had already had its bye week.

Should O'Connell ultimately name Cousins starter ahead of Sunday's kickoff at Lambeau Field, the 38-year-old could potentially end up playing an 18-game regular season.

articles.title: Travis Kelce’s Kansas City bachelor pad years: The home that became famous for parties, game nights, and Super Bowl celebrations
articles.summary: Travis Kelce bought a custom-built home in Kansas City's Briarcliff West in 2019 for $995,000, and for a few years it was where the Chiefs tight end lived
articles.body: Travis Kelce bought a custom-built home in Kansas City's Briarcliff West in 2019 for $995,000, and for a few years it was where the Chiefs tight end lived as a single man at the top of his game. Fans and photographers soon made it hard to live in. In late 2023 he moved to a gated estate in Leawood, Kansas, for a reported $6 million. That second house later hosted his proposal to Taylor Swift.Inside Travis Kelce's Kansas City bachelor pad in Briarcliff WestKelce did not start out in a mansion. Property reports also link him to a downtown high-rise called One Light Luxury, which came before the Briarcliff West purchase. Briarcliff West was his first real home in the city.Reports disagree on the size. Elle Decor describes a 10,000-square-foot residence with seven bedrooms and five bathrooms. Realtor.com has called it a 4,200-square-foot home. I could not settle that gap from public records, so treat any single figure with care.The amenities are less disputed. Coverage of his portfolio lists a wine cellar, a pool and a theater room, and another report adds a state-of-the-art gym. It is the kind of house built for having people over. That detail matters for the next question.Did the house really host the parties and game nights?Here the legend runs ahead of the record. Some lifestyle sites say Kelce often had teammates over for game nights and cookouts. Those claims come with no named guests, no dates and no firsthand accounts, so I would not lean on them.What is documented happened elsewhere. After the Chiefs beat the 49ers in overtime in Super Bowl LVIII, it was their third title in five years. The celebrations were in Las Vegas. Rolling Stone reported that Kelce, Patrick Mahomes and about 30 teammates went to XS Nightclub. A year later, after the AFC title game in January 2025, Kelce and Swift hosted a private rooftop party in Kansas City. That was a rented venue, not his living room.So the honest version is this. The house had every feature a host would want, and Kelce has a famously social reputation. The biggest nights, though, were public and mostly off his property.Why Kelce left the bachelor pad for LeawoodThe move was about privacy. One report said the old home was too accessible, and the stream of fans and photographers became overwhelming. He had been linked to Swift for only weeks when the Leawood purchase surfaced in October 2023. The home sits in a gated community about 15 miles from Arrowhead Stadium.The new place is a different scale. It spans about 17,000 square feet across nearly 3.5 acres. It was first listed in September 2022 at $6.9 million, so the reported price was a discount. The grounds include a lighted tennis and pickleball court, a mini golf course with a practice green, bridges, winding paths and a gazebo. Another report adds a gym and a sauna.Kelce never publicly confirmed the sale at the time. The Briarcliff West house appears to still be his. One estimate puts its value at just over $1 million, which suggests it has barely appreciated since 2019.What the Leawood house means nowThe Leawood property has already become part of the couple's story. In August 2025, Swift and Kelce announced their engagement, and Kelce's father said the proposal took place in the garden of his son's home. Kelce said afterward, "I'm an emotional guy". The city of Leawood put out a statement welcoming the attention.The couple married on July 3, 2026, at Madison Square Garden in New York. For now, a source told Page Six that Leawood is their primary residence while he is still playing for the Chiefs. That fits his schedule. Kelce signed a three-year extension in March, so he is under contract in Kansas City for years.Their plans may not stay in Kansas. Hello reported that Kelce bought a $5.35 million mansion near his hometown of Cleveland Heights, Ohio, on 3.5 acres. That detail comes from one outlet. The Leawood house has the contract, the proposal garden and the gates. The Ohio home may decide where they eventually settle.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Matt LaFleur surprised Vikings didn't have to give up more in Kirk Cousins trade: 'I was shocked'
articles.summary: Matt LaFleur would have loved to see the Vikings part with more in exchange for Kirk Cousins.
articles.body:
Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings and the rest of the NFC North is on high alert. The Vikings have already shown the division what its dominant defense can do, just imagine how the team will perform with a functional offense.

Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur will get his first look at the Vikings' revamped offense in Week 10. LaFleur is well aware what Cousins can bring to the table and admitted he was surprised the Vikings didn't have to give up more to bring Cousins back.

The Vikings managed to acquire Cousins on Tuesday for a 2027 third-round pick. With the move, the Raiders can now turn things over to No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza.

LaFleur had nothing but positive things to say about Cousins, calling him "a really intelligent guy" who has been "playing at a high level."

LaFleur then put the focus on the Las Vegas Raiders, saying he was surprised the team didn't get more in exchange for Cousins.

"I was surprised [the Raiders] didn't get more for him, quite honestly. I was shocked when I saw what they traded him for. It was mind-blowing to me."

The Packers' coach didn't mention the Vikings in his comments — or the Raiders, for that matter — but the implication was clear: He felt Minnesota should have been forced to part with more in exchange for Cousins.

That shouldn't necessarily come as a surprise. Cousins undoubtedly improves the Vikings in 2026 and makes the team a more legitimate Super Bowl contender. That could come at the expense of the Packers, who are fighting hard to remain in an exceptionally tough NFC North. Given all that, it's understandable why LaFleur would want to see a division rival part with more talent or higher draft picks in any trade.

Whether Cousins draws the start for the Vikings in Week 10 remains an open question. There are already reports suggesting that will be the case, as Cousins is still familiar with the team's offense. LaFleur certainly expects to see Cousins under center Sunday.

Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell isn't willing to make that commitment yet, saying the team would like that outcome, but wants to make sure Cousins is comfortable.

That sounds like an honest answer from O'Connell, though there could be a fair amount of gamesmanship in there.

Whether or not Cousins takes the field against the Packers in Week 10, LaFleur knows how much the veteran quarterback improves the Vikings. That's not a good thing for the Packers — or any team in the NFC North — which explains why LaFleur wishes Minnesota gave up more in the deal.

articles.title: In return to NFL coverage, Dianna Russini doesn’t address Mike Vrabel relationship
articles.summary: Diana Russini returned to covering the NFL on Wednesday with a new show, but did not address the relationship with New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel that cost her her perch as one of the league’s most high-profile reporters.
articles.body: Diana Russini returned to covering the NFL on Wednesday with a new show, but did not address the relationship with New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel that cost her her perch as one of the league’s most high-profile reporters. Seven months after the New York Post published photos of Russini and Vrabel together at an Arizona resort, and Russini resigned from her job at The Athletic amid an investigation by the outlet into her previous coverage, she announced this week a new show hosted by BetUS, an online betting sportsbook. “The Russini Report” was scheduled to air live at 12 p.m. ET Wednesday but did not air for at least 45 minutes, when a full version of the episode was uploaded. On social media, some users said that the BetUS site would not load, or that the stream had crashed. “Well... you broke it,” wrote the X account associated with Russini’s show. In a column on the BetUS website, Russini had written that “I have a lot to say” about her seven months away from coverage of the NFL. But when her show began, before appearances by guests including former NFL coach Bill Parcells, Russini did not address Vrabel, the nature of their relationship, or her decision to resign from The Athletic, instead offering “a personal note.” “You know, over the last few months, I have had a lot of time to think about my life and my priorities and the person I want to be moving forward and being home in New Jersey with my husband and our two little boys and being truly present. It gave me so much perspective that I didn’t even know I needed,” Russini said. “I’ve also had a lot of long conversations with people all around football. You know, some were about the game, and others were just about life. To the people who picked up the phone and checked in and offered both encouragement and honest advice, from the bottom of my heart, thank you. Those conversations helped me find my way back to the work I love and back to myself, right here hosting the show. “So, anyone who knows me knows I have always been obsessed with the NFL. But maybe because I wasn’t around it so much the last few months, my passion for covering this league has never been stronger. I’m so grateful, so grateful for this chance to do it again.” Russini became a national reporter while working at ESPN before joining The Athletic in 2023, where she wrote columns, hosted a podcast and was one of the company’s most-visible and highest-paid reporters, reported the New York Times, which owns The Athletic. Russini had not spoken publicly since issuing statements in April after the New York Post published photos of her and Vrabel together in Sedona. The Post published subsequent photos of the two in other locations. Vrabel missed the third day of the NFL draft in April to attend counseling with the Patriots’ support. After the photos were published, Vrabel told reporters at the time he’d “had some difficult conversations with people I care about — with my family, the organization, the coaches, the players.” Less than a week after the initial Post story, Russini resigned from The Athletic, writing “I have covered the NFL with professionalism and dedication throughout my career, and I stand behind every story I have ever published” in a letter to the publication’s top editor. An internal investigation by The Athletic ended in September and determined that although there were no clear links of bias showing that Russini’s coverage helped promote Vrabel, she had a “clear conflict of interest” that was not disclosed to her editors but should have been. “The appearances surrounding her relationship with Vrabel undermines our audience’s confidence in her impartiality,” the report’s author wrote.

articles.title: Everything Kirk Cousins Said About Vikings Trade, Raiders, Jakobe Thomas' No. 8 Jersey
articles.summary: Kirk Cousins is back in a familiar place after the Las Vegas Raiders traded him to the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for a third-round draft pick on Tuesday, but he wanted to offer his appreciation to his previous organization before fully looking ahead to his new one.
articles.body:
Kirk Cousins is back in a familiar place after the Las Vegas Raiders traded him to the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for a third-round draft pick on Tuesday, but he wanted to offer his appreciation to his previous organization before fully looking ahead to his new one.

"I want to say thank you to the Raiders for the opportunity they gave me this past offseason," the veteran quarterback told reporters Wednesday. "The chance they gave me to play and the way they handled with Minnesota the last 24 hours. So grateful for them and the people there, and certainly, it was tough to leave a building that you've spent some time with the guys and built some rapport."

This is something of a full-circle moment for Cousins, as he played in Minnesota from 2018 through 2023 and was a three-time Pro Bowler who threw for more than 4,000 yards in four different seasons.

He and go-to receiver Justin Jefferson already have chemistry in place, and he is ready to once again take the field for the NFC North team.

"You imagine it," he said of returning to the Vikings. "I don't know if you thought it was going to happen, but here we are. Grateful for the opportunity."

The reunion is also notable because he revealed he plays his "best when there is a lot of joy."

Cousins might get even more joy if he can play with his familiar No. 8, although that could be an issue since it belongs to rookie safety Jakobe Thomas in Minnesota. The quarterback addressed that and said , "I'm confident that Jakobe and I can have a healthy, mature conversation and figure this out."

Las Vegas deciding to move on from Cousins wasn't that surprising considering it selected Fernando Mendoza with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft. It was eventually going to give him the opportunity to prove himself as the franchise quarterback, and Cousins was essentially a placeholder this season.

While the Raiders are 4-5 and in the AFC playoff race, the Vikings also offered a solid draft pick as they attempt to address a major area of need.

With Kyler Murray sidelined by a hamstring injury, Carson Wentz threw for 81 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions in Monday's loss to the Buffalo Bills. Murray hasn't exactly been excellent either with five touchdown passes to three interceptions in six games.

Minnesota's dominant defense is talented enough to win a Super Bowl following a 6-2 start, but it needs better quarterback play if that is going to happen.

Enter Cousins, who is familiar with the system and some of the personnel. He should elevate the ceiling and will immediately be put to the test when the Vikings face the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on Sunday.

That is where he tore his Achilles in 2023, and he told reporters Wednesday playing there again "has meaning, but we have to make it mean something with the way you play."

The NFL world will be tuned in Sunday to see how he does play as he returns to a familiar club.

articles.title: Carson Beck Named Cardinals' QB1 vs. Matthew Stafford, Rams After Gardner Minshew Injury
articles.summary: It's Carson Beck time.
articles.body:
As expected, Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur confirmed to reporters on Wednesday that the rookie quarterback will get the start on Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams.

"You never really know until you get to the live bullets on Sunday," LaFleur told reporters regarding Beck getting his first start. "But just the way he goes about his business, whether it's been from OTAs through training camp before he got hurt, obviously, seeing him operate there in that first half plus the one possession in the second half [of the Hall of Fame game]. So, obviously we'll know more come Sunday, but have all the confidence he's ready to roll."

Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love has struggled with injuries. Wideout Michael Wilson is done for the season due to a fracture in his neck. Marvin Harrison Jr. fell so out of favor in the team's offense that he was traded to the Houston Texans, just three years after being the No. 4 overall pick. Quarterback Jacoby Brissett was dealt to the Baltimore Ravens last week. His replacement, Gardner Minshew II, likely requires surgery on his right ulnar collateral ligament that would end his season.

The result has been a 3-6 record and likely a fifth straight season without a playoff berth.

The upside is that the Cardinals are going to get a long look at Beck to see if they feel he has franchise-quarterback upside. The 23-year-old, a third-round pick in this year's draft, threw for 3,813 yards, 30 touchdowns and 12 interceptions in his final season at Miami, completing 72.4 percent of his passes.

Given how depleted the team's receiving corps is, it won't be the most accurate assessment of his potential. Expect Trey McBride to be a very busy man. And an opening showdown against a loaded Los Angeles Rams' defense is a rough introduction.

But if Beck thrives given the circumstances, the Cardinals will know that they have a player worth building around.

"Just go out and operate—go operate this offense and go play each play as its own," LaFleur said of his message to Beck. "Do what he's been doing in practice. It's just an extension of the practice field. Obviously, it's live bullets and go operate. Go play this game."

articles.title: Dianna Russini Addresses Hiatus in Video for New NFL Show After Investigation on Vrabel
articles.summary: Longtime NFL insider Dianna Russini said she gained a new perspective after her break from the sports media world.
articles.body:
Longtime NFL insider Dianna Russini said she gained a new perspective after her break from the sports media world.

Russini debuted her new show with BetUS on Wednesday. During the first episode, she addressed the multiple months she was away from her usual duties. She said she benefited from "being truly present" with her husband and two children.

Russini added she had conversations with people around the NFL, which "helped me find my way back to the work I love."

Tomlin Focused on Broadcasting, Not Coaching

Russini resigned from The Athletic in April after the company launched an investigation into photos of her and New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel at a resort in Sedona, Arizona.

Speaking with Page Six , the outlet that published the photos, Russini said the pictures "don't represent the group of six people who were hanging out during the day." Vrabel, for his part, said they "show a completely innocent interaction and any suggestion otherwise is laughable."

Vrabel briefly stepped away from the Patriots, missing the third day of the 2026 NFL draft so that he could attend counseling.

BetUS announced Monday that Russini will have a weekly show and column with the online sportsbook.

"I'm excited to get back to reporting on the NFL and bring that passion to BetUS," she said in the press release. "I want to give fans more than just the headlines, sharing insider perspectives, uncovering the stories behind the biggest moments, and helping audiences better understand the teams, players, and matchups that shape each week."

articles.summary: Los peatones tenían la preferencia de paso al cruzar una calle y llegaron a fotografiar el vehículo de Ryan
articles.body: El exentrenador de la NFL, Rex Ryan, se ha entregado a la policía este miércoles tras supuestamente atropellar a dos peatones con su coche en Nashville y darse a la fuga. La policía de Nashville ha informado que los sucesos tuvieron lugar la pasada semana y que los peatones tenían la preferencia de paso al cruzar una calle principal en el centro de la ciudad. Ryan supuestamente giró con el semáforo en rojo y las ruedas de su vehículo pasaron por encima de los pies de dos personas. Pese a todo, los peatones lograron alcanzar al conductor cuando se encontraba detenido en un semáforo en rojo. En ese momento se produjo una discusión verbal, durante la cual el exentrenador bajó de su vehículo. Ryan se habría marchado sin proporcionar información ni ofrecer ayuda, aunque sí se tomó una foto de su coche. Ryan ha sido acusado de abandonar el lugar del accidente, de no proporcionar información ni prestar auxilio y de no obedecer una señal de control de tráfico. En total se trata de seis cargos de delitos menores. Ryan, que ahora es analista de ESPN, tendrá que comparecer ante el tribunal el mes que viene. Rex Ryan fue entrenador jefe de los New York Jets desde 2009 hasta 2014 y de los Buffalo Bills desde 2015 hasta 2016. Llevó a los Jets a dos finales consecutivas del campeonato de la AFC tras las temporadas de 2009 y 2010. Desde que dejó de entrenar, Ryan ha trabajado como analista de la NFL para ESPN.

articles.title: Puka Nacua, Davante Adams Injuries, Return Timelines Updated by Rams' Sean McVay
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua, who suffered a sprained MCL and PCL sprain in his right knee as well as turf toe on the final offensive snap of his team's 20-13 road win over the Washington Commanders last Sunday, is expected to be out for a "significant period of time," per head coach Sean McVay to reporters on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua, who suffered a sprained MCL and PCL sprain in his right knee as well as turf toe on the final offensive snap of his team's 20-13 road win over the Washington Commanders last Sunday, is expected to be out for a "significant period of time," per head coach Sean McVay to reporters on Wednesday.

However, Nacua won't be going on injured reserve, per McVay, "because of some semantics with the roster."

There's good news regarding wideout Davante Adams, who is dealing with a ruptured semitendinosus (hamstring muscle on the back of the thigh) and hasn't played since Oct. 18.

Rams to Consider Trade After Puka Injury

McVay told reporters that the Rams hope to get him back after the team plays the Green Bay Packers on Wed., Nov. 25. If he returns then, Adams would miss just two more games (Sunday at Arizona Cardinals plus Packers) and get back on Thursday, Dec. 3 vs. the Kansas City Chiefs.

ESPN's Dan Graziano had an interesting theory as to why the Rams may not have placed Nacua on injured reserve. In essence, placing him on injured reserve would mean Nacua misses four games at minimum. However, the Rams reportedly have hope he can return for Week 14. If that's the case, Nacua would only miss three games since L.A. has a Week 11 bye.

"Being on IR means you must miss at least four games, not weeks, and the Rams have a bye in Week 11. So if they think it's possible Nacua might only have to miss four weeks, they could refrain from putting him on IR and possibly have him back in time for their Week 14 game at San Francisco. This all becomes moot if they put Nacua on IR this week, but just keep an eye on the situation if they don't. Speaking to people close to this situation Monday evening, they were very adamant that Nacua's injury isn't season-ending and that they hope to get him back for Week 14 or 15."

The Rams certainly hope Nacua is back sooner rather than later. He's averaging 10 catches per game (70 receptions in seven games) this season. Nacua has also amassed 715 receiving yards and four touchdowns.

Adams has also been productive, accumulating 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdowns. Thankfully, it's possible he only misses two more games, and either way, it appears he'll be available for the final regular season stretch.

In the meantime, the Rams forge ahead without both players. L.A. still thankfully has a healthy backfield (QB Matthew Stafford, running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum). Tight end Tyler Higbee is the team's available leading pass-catcher. L.A. will also call on the likes of wide receivers Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield.

There's no lingering tension between new San Francisco 49ers teammates Keenan Allen and Mike Evans after they made some pointed remarks toward one another years ago.

Allen, who joined the Niners ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, told reporters he and Evans resolved their differences "a long time ago." He also quipped that Evans is the better receiver "at this point."

That's not how Allen felt ahead of the 2020 season, and he said so publicly. That inevitably drew the ire of Evans:

It doesn't appear the beef between Allen and Evans went any deeper than where they resided in the annual NFL Top 100 for 2020.

That's nothing compared to the trash talk Richard Sherman dished out toward San Francisco during his seven years with the Seattle Seahawks. Sherman went on to have a solid run in the Bay Area.

The 49ers turned to Allen to provide depth to an injury-ravaged receiver room.

Ricky Pearsall underwent season-ending surgery before the campaign kicked off. Second-round draft pick De'Zhaun Stribling is recovering from the ankle injury he suffered in Week 1. Christian Kirk has likewise been limited to one appearance. Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. were sidelined for the 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 9.

Allen, a six-time Pro Bowler, has clearly lost a step. But his 40 receptions with the Indianapolis Colts are more than any 49ers player, and he'd be third on the team in receiving yards (351).

The 34-year-old could make a real difference for the offense in the second half of the schedule.

articles.title: Cardinals to start rookie QB Carson Beck vs. Rams following Gardner Minshew injury, Jacoby Brissett trade
articles.summary: It's Beck's turn to pilot Arizona's offense under first-year head coach Mike LaFleur; however, he'll be working with a shorthanded unit.
articles.body:
At 3-6, and with a rash of injuries — including one to their most recent starting quarterback — the Arizona Cardinals are turning to rookie Carson Beck.

Arizona benched and then traded Jacoby Brissett . His replacement, Gardner Minshew, suffered a UCL injury this past week in Seattle during a loss to the Seahawks.

In their absence, the No. 65 overall pick in this year's draft is getting the nod in the desert.

Beck will make his first career NFL start on Sunday when the Los Angeles Rams come to town, head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday.

"I know this isn't too big for him," said LaFleur, who voiced that he wants the soon-to-be 25-year-old to let it rip.

The former Georgia and Miami star will be tasked with moving the ball against a defense that features premier edge rusher Myles Garrett and stout defensive tackle Aaron Donald. Beck will have to do so with a thin receiving corps.

Although tight end Trey McBride — who's first among all NFL players this season with 73 receptions — will serve as a nice security blanket for the third-round pick, Beck will be working with a group of wide receivers that's currently led by the likes of Reggie Virgil, Simi Fehoko and Devin Duvernay.

Altogether, that trio has combined for 1,235 career receiving yards, and Duvernay has accounted for 1,025 of those. He's a two-time Pro Bowler but for his return skills.

It's possible Zay Jones is pulled up from the practice squad. Either way, it'll be a lot more difficult for the Cardinals to evaluate what they really have in Beck at this point, especially compared to earlier this season when they had Michael Wilson, Marvin Harrison Jr. and Kendrick Bourne lining up at wide receiver.

Wilson, the team's WR1, is out for the season with a neck injury he sustained in Seattle this past weekend . Arizona dealt Harrison to the Houston Texans last month in Week 5 . As for Bourne, he went down with a serious ankle injury during the Cardinals' Week 8 road win over the Dallas Cowboys.

Plus, Jalen Brooks — a 2023 seventh-round pick who impressed in the preseason and recently began making a regular-season impact — is done for the year due to a wrist injury he experienced in a Week 7 loss to the Denver Broncos.

Not only will Beck be playing with a hodgepodge of wideouts, but he'll also be quarterbacking behind an offensive line that's been missing left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. The blind-side protector landed on season-ending injured reserve after he tore his left biceps amid a Week 4 road defeat to the New York Giants.

And, to top it off, a notable draft classmate of Beck's, Jeremiyah Love, is currently on IR. The highly touted running back, this year's No. 3 overall pick, is dealing with his latest ankle issue .

On the bright side, Beck played outstanding in his lone preseason appearance . He got the start in the Hall of Fame Game, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown on 15-of-19 passing against the Carolina Panthers.

Granted it was the Hall of Fame Game, but Virgil showcased some chemistry with Beck while Fehoko caught Beck's TD pass.

Those former scout team receivers are now part of a first-string offense that Beck will be commanding on Sunday.

"He was mature when he got here," LaFleur said of Beck on Wednesday. "Miami and Georgia, I think he was in two really good environments, two really good cultures to prep him for these kind of moments, whether it be in college and then in the NFL.

"So he's been a pro since he's been here. He puts in the exact amount of work that he needs."

Beck has spent most of the season behind a pair of QBs. Yet Brissett, who started the Cardinals' first eight games, is now on the Baltimore Ravens, and Minshew, Arizona's pick to start last week in Seattle, is on IR.

Perhaps it's fitting that Beck and Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza will each get their first career NFL start on Sunday , as they concluded their college careers facing off in the national championship.

"I think you learn through experience, but you also learn through watching other people do it, good and bad," LaFleur said, when asked about first-year signal-callers having time to sit before their number is called.

"So for Carson and having to watch Kirk Cousins over in Vegas with Mendoza, those are beneficial times. But, again, being out there and having to do it is the key."

articles.body: Travis Kelce has spent years making headlines for his achievements on the football field. But one of his most meaningful contributions came away from the stadium. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end saw an opportunity to change young lives in his community and decided to act. Kelce wanted to help bridge that gap by giving teenagers a safe place to explore their interests and develop skills that could help them build independent futures.The Ignition Lab officially opened in 2021. Rather than simply telling young people to dream big, the project gave them a place to start working towards those ambitions.Travis Kelce's Ignition Lab is helping students discover their potentialThe impact of the project goes beyond the building itself. articles.title: Mississippi State’s Kamario Taylor finalizing a reported $7.5 million deal, in wild college football move
articles.summary: Kamario Taylor's reported $7.5 million deal to stay at Mississippi State could reach $9 million with bonuses, matching mid first-round draft money.
articles.body: How much will it take for college football programs to re-sign their top quarterbacks heading into the 2027 season? Just ask Mississippi State's Kamario Taylor. We have entered new territory when it comes to paying college athletes, especially in this era of NIL and revenue-sharing that has transcended the sports world. College quarterbacks are making upwards of $6 to $7 million this season to lead their respective teams on the field, with that number only growing over the next few years as the price continues to trend upwards. If you want an example of how much college sports have turned into a professional model, Mississippi State is finalizing a new deal with star quarterback Kamario Taylor that On3 reported will pay him $7.5 million next season for his services, and that number could jump to around $9 million if he collects incentive bonuses. 'Super-Kamario' did not want to leave the Bulldogs for another school Wanting to stay Starkville has always been a priority for Taylor, who spent a lot of time before even enrolling at Mississippi State cheering on the Bulldogs. But, the ongoing talking-points around the sport of college football have centered around why Kamario should go chase a bigger paycheck somewhere else following the 2026 season. "When I got to Mississippi State, I knew we could build something special," Kamario Taylor said in a statement on Wednesday. "These last few weeks have only made me want it more. And I promise you this - big things are ahead for this program. Believe that. We have major goals, and we're here to win. There's no question that we understand the expectations, the standard and what it's going to take to get there. And I couldn't be hungrier for it."Right now, I wish more than anything I could be out on that field with my brothers. But I know they'll keep putting in the work to finish this season strong. My recovery is right on track, and I'm looking forward to the day that I get to go back to work with these guys and the future talent that will be coming to Starkville." BYU HAS THRIVED IN AN NIL ERA THAT MANY EXPECTED THEM TO FALTER IN, NFL LEGEND STEVE YOUNG SAYS Whether it was numerous media pundits floating the idea that he would be happier somewhere else other than Starkville, the Bulldogs quarterback made it known to the coaching staff that he did not want to play elsewhere next season, and he wasn’t chasing the 'bag'. But, that didn’t mean Mississippi State donors weren’t going to make sure their talented quarterback wasn’t taken care of from a financial standpoint, and they weren’t going to take the risk of some other team making him think twice about his decision. COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S JERRY JONES? TEXAS TECH BOOSTER CODY CAMPBELL DEMANDS RETURN ON INVESTMENT This is a growing trend in college athletics. Conference commissioners and school officials can lobby all they want about reigning in the sport, but money will continue to talk. And, if you think some schools are going to sit by and watch others swoop in to steal their talented players, you don't understand the pull that a place like Mississippi State can put together to entice athletes to stay. "I can't wait to play for Coach Lebby in 2027. He believed in me from day one, and I believe in where he's taking this program," Kamario Taylor mentioned about head coach Jeff Lebby. "I'm grateful to Mr. Selmon and the leadership at Mississippi State for their commitment to building a winning program here.
