articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza is grateful for his time working under former mentor Kirk Cousins, who was traded to the Minnesota Vikings on Tuesday after nine games with the Silver and Black.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza is grateful for his time working under former mentor Kirk Cousins, who was traded to the Minnesota Vikings on Tuesday after nine games with the Silver and Black.

"I wanted to make a statement where I really, truly from the bottom of my heart wanted to thank Kirk and the entire Cousins family, whether it's Julie, Cooper, Turner," Mendoza said during his press conference with reporters on Wednesday.

"They've, as a family, done so much for me. They've essentially taken me into their household when they were here, and they welcomed me with open arms.

"It would've been really easy for Kirk to, you know, being a veteran quarterback and kind of already have proven everything to be a little bit more dismissive, but he had me with open arms and has taught me so many things, whether it's film study, how to operate as a starting quarterback, all the different multifaceted approaches that has made him so successful throughout his career, he has shared with no restrictions or no constraints.

"So I really appreciate him, and it was heartfelt to see him. He was a great mentor."

In early April, the Raiders signed Cousins to a one-year deal as essentially a bridge quarterback before their future franchise signal-caller took the reins.

A few weeks later, the Raiders did the inevitable and selected Mendoza, the reigning Heisman Trophy winner and a national champion at Indiana, with the No. 1 overall pick in this year's draft.

Cousins did well as the Raiders' quarterback, and he's currently second in the NFL with 20 touchdown passes and fifth with 2,340 passing yards. However, he's back in Minnesota, where he spent the 2018-2023 seasons.

The timing seems right, as Mendoza wasn't thrust into the spotlight right away and got a great chance to learn under Cousins, who now gets a chance to lead a 6-2 team fighting for the playoffs and potentially a Super Bowl.

Mendoza's first start will be Sunday at home against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.

articles.title: Harrison Butker's Status as Chiefs Kicker Updated by Andy Reid Amid Latest Struggles
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have no plans to make a change at kicker despite Harrison Butker suffering through his worst season so far.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs have no plans to make a change at kicker despite Harrison Butker suffering through his worst season so far.

Coach Andy Reid told reporters Wednesday that Butker will remain the starter.

"Harrison has done such a great job for us over time here," Reid said. "Sometimes you go through these little peaks-and-valleys things. I've got to give him a chance to work through them, and we'll see how things go. We'll just take it week by week."

Butker is 12-of-19 on field goals in 2026, and his seven misses are already a career high.

In the 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos, Butker couldn't connect on a 54-yard attempt in the fourth quarter. That proved costly as the Chiefs were driving for the game-winning score on the final drive and needed a touchdown instead of a field goal.

Kansas City rebounded with a 35-12 victory over the New York Jets, but the Arrowhead Stadium crowd made their voices heard when Butker had another field goal sail wide at the end of the first half. It immediately followed a missed attempt that didn't count due to an offsides penalty.

Immediately after the Jets game, Reid was noncommittal about his kicker situation heading into Week 10. The Chiefs signed seven-time Pro Bowler Justin Tucker to their practice squad, so they have a replacement waiting in the wings.

Tucker hasn't suited up since the 2024 season, and he similarly hit a nadir that year. His 73.3 percent success rate was a personal low. The 36-year-old may not actually be much of an upgrade.

At a certain point, Butker won't leave Reid with much of a choice if his struggles to continue. For now, he's being afforded every opportunity to get things right.

articles.title: Duke Tobin sends out 'not comfortable' head coach Zac Taylor to explain Bengals' trade-deadline snafu with Eagles
articles.summary: Zac Taylor almost certainly had little to nothing to do with the trade-deadline snafu in which the Bengals backed out of an agreed-upon deal with the Eagles....
articles.body:
Zac Taylor almost certainly had little to nothing to do with the trade-deadline snafu on Tuesday in which the Cincinnati Bengals backed out of an agreed-upon deal with the Philadelphia Eagles.

On Wednesday, the Bengals' head coach took the podium to discuss the topic despite declaring that he was "not comfortable" doing so. He said he did it at the behest of director of player personnel and de facto general manager Duke Tobin.

Per Taylor, Tobin is "really apologetic." To be clear, that came from Taylor's mouth, not Tobin's.

"Obviously, we tried something yesterday," Taylor said. "Duke was very explicit with me when he came and spoke to me of how he wanted this portrayed. I'm not comfortable doing it, but I'm going to do what he asked.

"We did make an effort to kind of put some depth in there in place of Cashius [Howell]. As we got into it, obviously it was going to be a little more costly than we initially anticipated. He's really apologetic about it and wants to make clear: Philly was a great trade partner. It was on our end."

Embarrassing oversight by Bengals front office

In case you missed it, the Bengals had an agreement with the Eagles in place to acquire edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie prior to Tuesday's trade deadline. The Bengals need depth at the position due to a wrist injury that placed Howell on injured reserve.

In the agreed upon deal, the Bengals would've sent a sixth-round pick to the Eagles and received Ebiketie in return. But it turns out the deal came at a significantly higher cost, which the Bengals' front office apparently didn't realize when it made the agreement.

Per the NFL's compensatory picks mechanisms, the Bengals would've also had to forfeit a third-round compensatory pick to acquire Ebiketie. So in essence, they would have parted with a third-round pick and a sixth-round pick to acquire a backup pass rusher.

It's a price that's prohibitive and one the Bengals reportedly didn't realize until Over the Cap's self-proclaimed "Compensatory Picks Guy™" Nick Korte pointed it out on social media .

Korte's analysis picked up traction among traditional NFL media, and only then did the Bengals back out of the deal , having realized its true cost.

This was all reported Tuesday, and Taylor was left to confirm it with media on Wednesday.

This is not Taylor's job. He's a head football coach. He's not supposed to be tasked with knowing the complex mechanics of NFL trades or the league's compensatory pick system, and he's not the one who pulled the trigger on the agreement with the Eagles.

Those responsibilities lie with the player personnel arm of Cincinnati's front office, which is run by Tobin. The mistake was an embarrassment for Tobin's department that played out across sports media on Tuesday.

On Wednesday, Tobin sent out Taylor to face the music.

articles.summary: Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck explained that he isn't nervous heading into the first start of his career.
articles.body:
Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck explained that he isn't nervous heading into the first start of his career.

"The coolest thing about confidence is confidence is a choice," Beck said Wednesday, per Darren Urban of the team's official website.

The 2026 third-round pick has operated in a depth role for Arizona to begin this season, but Cardinals head coach Matt LaFleur named Beck as the starter for a Week 10 clash with the Los Angeles Rams after veteran passer Gardner Minshew suffered a UCL injury .

Beck also discussed facing an imposing Rams defensive front that features Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald.

"What they're able to do on defense, it causes problems for offenses," Beck told reporters (11:16 mark). "It's definitely gonna be a challenge for us. So I think the biggest thing is watching the film, seeing what we want to do and then ultimately trying to go out there and execute our plan."

Veteran signal-caller Jacoby Brissett opened the season as Arizona's starter under center, appearing in eight games before he was benched in favor of Minshew during a 33-30 win over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8.

The Cardinals eventually traded Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens on Friday.

Minshew started one game for Arizona before suffering the UCL injury in his throwing arm during a 17-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, dropping the team to 3-6.

Beck will now attempt to establish himself as the Cardinals' long-term answer at quarterback.

The 24-year-old wrapped up an impressive senior season at Miami in 2025, completing 72.4 percent of his throws for 3,813 yards and 30 touchdowns compared to 12 interceptions across 16 games. He helped the Hurricanes make an appearance in the College Football Playoff national championship game.

Beck went on to make one preseason appearance for the Cardinals this year, finishing 15-of-19 for 188 yards and one touchdown without getting picked off during a 33-30 loss to the Carolina Panthers on Aug. 6.

The Rams sit at 5-4 this season following a slow start to the year, but they've won three straight games and boast one of the NFL's top pass defenses. Los Angeles is allowing just 198.7 yards per game through the air, ranking No. 5 among all teams.

The Kansas City Chiefs tight end and his wife have secured approval for a fresh round of landscaping changes at their $5.35 million Ohio mansion, despite mounting objections from nearby residents. What began as a discussion about privacy and property improvements quickly turned into a heated neighborhood debate. Some residents questioned the scale of the proposed changes, while others argued that the couple deserved a warm welcome. In the end, the local review board sided with the revised plans.Travis Kelce's Ohio mansion renovation plans spark neighborhood backlashThe dispute took centre stage at a meeting of Bratenahl's Architectural Review Board on Tuesday, November 10. Around 35 people attended the gathering at the Bratenahl Community Center, where residents raised concerns about plans to surround the property with shrubs reaching 10 feet in height.For Kelce, privacy is an understandable concern. The NFL star and his wife purchased the eight-bedroom, 11-bathroom lakefront property for $5.35 million in March. However, some neighbours believe the proposed greenery could change the character of the area and affect local wildlife.Resident Lucy Weller questioned whether the landscaping would benefit the natural surroundings. She urged the couple's representatives to consider native plants and designs that support local animals.“Here is a wonderful opportunity for people who have money to put it into the caliber that this house should have,” Weller said. “I think this is a wonderful opportunity for this camp to go back and learn a bit about native species and designs that show what animals need in this area.”She also delivered a particularly blunt assessment of the proposed landscape.“They don’t need lawns; they need food and cover and they need places to have sex. I don’t think this landscape does anything to provide for any of the wildlife.”Another resident, Chuck Bauernschmidt, who lives two houses away, also questioned the changes. He said he felt “bad for the village” and argued that the property could end up looking more like a forest than a residential home.Travis Kelce gets approval despite criticism from Ohio residentsNot everyone at the meeting opposed the renovation. Several residents defended the couple, arguing that their decision to choose Bratenahl as a home deserved appreciation rather than criticism.Vasiliki Diamantis received applause after encouraging the community to welcome the high-profile residents.“We should feel privileged that these people chose this location for their residence and instead we are arguing over landscape and privacy as opposed to coming together as a community and looking at it as, ‘Wow, they chose Bratenahl, because Bratenahl is a special place,'” Diamantis said.She added, “We should accept them regardless of how many days they live here.”The debate also took an uncomfortable turn when one attendee predicted that the property would be sold within seven to 10 years following a possible divorce. The remark drew boos from the audience.Despite the disagreements, the board unanimously approved the revised landscaping plans, including the 10-foot shrubs and updated brickwork.The couple had previously received permission for a six-foot privacy fence in September after agreeing to reduce its proposed height from eight feet.Kelce and his wife were not present at the meeting. Their property manager Patrick Hyland, architect Derek Kuryla and project manager Jacob Kutz represented them.Although the mansion is receiving considerable attention, the property will reportedly not serve as the couple's primary residence. articles.title: New George Pickens Rumors Reveal Lack of Trade Interest in Cowboys WR Ahead of NFL Deadline
articles.summary: Even if the Dallas Cowboys had any interest in moving George Pickens ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, which they likely didn't, there reportedly wasn't much of a market awaiting them.
articles.body:
Even if the Dallas Cowboys had any interest in moving George Pickens ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, which they likely didn't, there reportedly wasn't much of a market awaiting them.

According to Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News , Pickens "wasn't as sought after by teams as some thought he would be. The franchise didn't receive phone calls about Pickens, two people with knowledge of the situation told the Dallas Morning News ."

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler also added that the Cowboys didn't receive calls regarding Pickens and that the wideout is "happy in Dallas and didn't want to be traded. Teams in the receiver market weren't shopping in the high-end aisle, either, so the idea of a Pickens trade was a nonstarter. Plus, Dallas had no plans to deal him."

While the Cowboys (4-5) are nowhere close to being a Super Bowl contender, they remains very much in the running for the NFC East crown behind the New York Giants (5-2-1). That always made Dallas an incredibly unlikely seller.

There's also the fact that Pickens is playing this season on the franchise tag and is a looming free agent. While other pending free agents at wideout were moved like Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, both went for far lower prices than the Cowboys would have demanded for Pickens. Plus, spending that type of future draft capital to acquire a player of his stature would have put pressure on the front office to either cave in to his contractual demands in the offseason or make peace with the situation being a very expensive short-term rental.

Neither scenario would be particularly ideal from a front-office perspective.

The least charitable (and incorrect) interpretation of his barren market is that NFL teams didn't feel he could positively impact their chances at contention. While Pickens isn't going to match last season's fantastic output (93 catches for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns), he's still on pace to eclipse 1,000 receiving yards this season, posting 39 catches for 533 yards and two scores through eight games.

That regression to the mean should have been somewhat expected. CeeDee Lamb remains an elite receiver and is having a fantastic season—he missed three games last season—and Pickens has very much been the WR2 in 2026.

But Pickens is still just 25 years old and has shown how much of a weapon he can be in the right scheme. NFL teams are assuredly intrigued by his talent, but it's easy enough to understand why they'd wait until he's a free agent to pursue him.

Just two weeks ago, Jacoby Brissett was starting at quarterback for the Arizona Cardinals. Midway through a Week 8 matchup, Brissett was replaced by Gardner Minshew, who led the team to a high-scoring victory in overtime. Minshew Mania is always fun, but it didn't last. During his first start of the season, the mustached man under center suffered a UCL injury that could sideline him for the rest of the year.

That means it is Carson Beck's time to shine. The rookie third-rounder was a two-time national champion at Georgia. However, those wins had more to do with the players around him than they did because he is the next big thing in the NFL. In fact, Beck was a backup on those Georgia championship teams. Beck did show some flashes during the preseason, but coming off the trade deadline, he ranks as the second-worst starting QB in the NFL because he has zero regular season throws and many experts don't peg him as a starting-caliber player.

Like the Cardinals, the Philadelphia Eagles are on their third starting quarterback, too. The difference is that the Eagles' initial starter, Jalen Hurts, would have ranked much higher on this list than anyone who has suited up for Arizona. A blood clot scare has the former Super Bowl MVP shut down for the year.

Tanner McKee was the next man up, but poor play led to the Eagles giving Joe Milton a chance. Milton isn't known for having great accuracy or the best anticipation, but man does he have a cannon for an arm. The 6-foot-5, 236 pounder is a physical specimen who famously can throw a football around 70 yards from his knees.

This elite arm strength alone gives Milton immense potential. There is obviously a lot more to football than throwing bullets, though. In his first career start, Milton went 18-for-34 for 169 yards and no touchdowns, proving that he is not the complete quarterback package. If Milton remains under center for the rest of the season, he is sure to have a couple of highlight deep balls, but as an overall starting quarterback, he is one of the worst in the league.

The Atlanta Falcons had Cooper Rush, Tua Tagovailoa, and Jack Strand keep the quarterback seat warm in Atlanta until Michael Penix Jr. was able to return to action. Quarterback play certainly has been better with the Washington product, but Penix's streakiness keeps him low in these QB rankings.

While Penix did have back-to-back three-touchdown performances in Weeks 6 and 7, he followed that up with a four-interception game in which he went eight-for-24. That nightmare of a game, which came in bad weather, doesn't define Penix's season, but he has a relatively weak arm and has been unwilling to make plays down the field. Penix ranks as the 29th quarterback the rest of the season.

J.J. McCarthy had to exit the New York Giants' Week 9 game, and he went viral for the severe pain he appeared to be in. However, McCarthy is seemingly set to return to action for New York's Week 10 game that will occur during Thursday Night Football. Despite being a bust who only lasted 10 starts with the team that drafted him in the first-round, McCarthy has surprisingly done a fair amount of winning in his career.

He has an 8-4 record, which includes wins in each of his past six starts. Of course, McCarthy won a national championship in college while at Michigan, too. Still, the production has left a lot to be desired, but with Jaxson Dart out for the year and Jameis Winston proving too streaky, McCarthy will likely have the rest of the season to demonstrate that he is a winner.

Jacoby Brissett ranked as the 29th-best quarterback coming into the season. He is up two spots now, despite having already been benched and traded to a new team. The improvement mainly comes because of injuries elsewhere around the league. With the Baltimore Ravens, Brissett will likely do what he always does, and that is nothing special, but nothing necessarily bad, either.

Of course, quickly learning a new play book is never easy, but Brissett is a high-IQ player who will definitely upgrade the Ravens' offense right away with Lamar Jackson hurt.

The Indianapolis Colts underwent a complete rebuild ahead of the NFL traded deadline, but they actually opted against moving Daniel Jones. The former number six pick was labeled a bust after stints with the Giants and Minnesota Vikings. Then, he reestablished himself in Indianapolis last season.

The Colts were even one of the top offenses in the league last year until Jones tore his achilles tendon. The back half of last season, and the first half of this one, have not been so pretty, though, and Jones has reminded fans of his old self. He has just six touchdowns to 10 interceptions on the year and should probably again be remembered as a draft bust.

Geno Smith was once viewed as the future of the New York Jets. He ended up becoming a long-term backup and a journeyman of sorts, but he also earned two Pro Bowl nods late in his career. Now in his 14th season, Smith is back in New York and actually putting up solid numbers. Smith's 2,078 passing yards rank 10th in the NFL, and he only has three interceptions.

Turnovers are something he has struggled with in the past, but not as much this year. While Smith is on pace for one of the best quarterbacking seasons in recent Jets' memory, it still feels like he is a stopgap option.

The Cleveland Browns entered the season with a quarterback competition between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders. Watson was once a Pro Bowl level player, but he had become more known these days for off-the-field controversies and being a part of one of the worst trades and one of the worst contracts in NFL history.

To make matters worse, Watson got on the Dawg Pound's bad side before the start of the season. Cleveland fans have had no choice but to embrace the quarterback ever since, though. The Browns keep winning games with Watson under center, something that most assumed would be infrequent after the Myles Garrett trade.

Now, Watson hasn't been great, but he has been clutch. He missed the last game with an injury, which allowed Sanders a chance to prove himself, but the team fell short, and Watson will be back under center going forward.

Cam Ward's stock is up slightly after a 304-yard, two-touchdown game in which the Tennessee Titans scored 36 points in an overtime loss. The Titans were desperate for a flash of superstardom like this from their 2025 first overall pick, but overall, Ward hasn't looked the part of the megastar the Titans needed when they drafted 1-1.

Week 9 was just his first of the season with multiple touchdown passes, and Ward has already attained a loser label. Tennessee's offense has been stagnant much more often than not. Still, there is loads of potential with Ward. In college, he was capable of throwing darts all over the field from different arm angles. Ward heated up during the back half of his rookie season. Perhaps that will be the case again this year. For now, though, fans have to worry that he is entering bust territory.

Sam Darnold is fresh off a Super Bowl victory. That ensured that them bust talk that plagued him early in his career became a thing of the past, as he'd instead been immortalized as an NFL legend. That doesn't mean Darnold is some elite NFL quarterback, though. The Seattle Seahawks QB ranks just 24th with 1,478 passing yards. His nine interceptions are the third most in the NFL, too.

Interceptions have long been Darnold's weak point. While he can whip the football all around the field, it far too often ends up in the hands of opposing defensive backs.

21. Justin Herbert, Los Angeles Chargers

Justin Herbert has gone crashing down the starting quarterback rankings. Herbert came into the NFL red hot. He has records for passing yards through two, three, four, and five seasons. However, seven seasons into his career and Herbert as zero playoff wins and just two Pro Bowls as his lone accolades to show for it.

This season has been particularly disastrous for Herbert. His Los Angeles Chargers are 0-8, and Herbert has just six touchdowns to a league-leading 11 interceptions. The 6-foot-6 quarterback has the potential to turn things around, and the Chargers certainly still view him as their franchise guy for now.

However, it appears that Herbert has lost all confidence, and this season has already been lost. Hopefully Herbert will show flashes of his old self during the back-half of the season. If not, there are going to be some tough questions to be had in Los Angeles.

Four MVPs, 10 Pro Bowls, and two seasons leading the NFL in passing touchdowns, and Aaron Rodgers ranks as just the 20th best quarterback in the NFL? That is right, as the 42-year-old just isn't the player he once was. Rodgers' long and successful career means he knows where the football needs to go, but his body is letting him down and prevents him from making the highlight plays that he became known for.

Rodgers isn't completely washed up. His Pittsburgh Steelers have won four straight games and lead the AFC North. There is no arguing that the future Hall of Famer is pretty mediocre at this point and most definitely a shell of his former self.

The New Orleans Saints turned a lot of heads when they drafted Tyler Shough 40th overall in 2025. He was slated to be a 26-year-old rookie; he had a lot of lowlight clips from college that went viral, and he was taken before the big-name that was Shedeur Sanders. The Saints have proven they made the right decision, though, as Shough has flashed franchise-level talent.

Shough has prototypical size and impressive arm strength. He needs to continue proving himself to make the jump into the top 16 on this list, though.

The number one pick will officially have his chance to shine. The Las Vegas Raiders drafted Fernando Mendoza first overall after he won the Heisman Trophy and led Indiana to the first 16-0 FBS season since the 1800s. The Raiders had Kirk Cousins on their roster to begin the year, but many projected the rookie would quickly take over. Instead, Cousins played too well.

The veteran was traded at the trade deadline, though, opening up the door for Mendoza to prove he can be a superstar. Of course, there will likely be rookie struggles, but Mendoza's poise and accuracy make it likely that he will be better off than most first-year signal-callers. With a lot of struggling quarterbacks league-wide, Mendoza slots in as QB18 before his first official NFL start.

17. Baker Mayfield, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

After a messy contract negotiation in the offseason, the expectation was that Baker Mayfield would be at his best in 2026. After all, he is a fiery quarterback who plays with a chip on his shoulder, and his best seasons have come with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Injuries have limited Mayfield to six games, though, and he has been pretty bad when he has been on the field.

The two-time Pro Bowler has just 922 yards for three touchdowns. That includes a zero completion game that actually ended up in a Tampa Bay win, a feat that hadn't been accomplished since 1974. Mayfield hates when he doesn't live up to his standards, and improvement over the back half of the season can be expected, especially with the NFC South so up for grabs.

The Las Vegas Raiders brought Kirk Cousins in to serve as the bridge quarterback and mentor for Fernando Mendoza until the number one pick was ready to go. Nearly everyone assumed that the rookie would have been handed the reins earlier now, but Cousins had played too well to be demoted.

In fact, Cousins is second in touchdowns (23) and fifth in passing yards (2,340). This is nothing new for Kirko Chains. When he has someone coming for his job, he tends to play lights out, but when he is comfortable, his play slips. Mendoza, fresh off one of the best collegiate seasons ever, is still the future of the franchise, and Cousins' excellent play garnered him plenty of trade value, so the Minnesota Vikings traded for the veteran at the trade deadline in hopes that he can fix their biggest issue.

The team's defense has been elite, but Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz have held them back. If Cousins continues the level of play he had in Las Vegas, Minnesota just may be legitimate contenders.

Bryce Young was handed the bust label quickly into his career, but he has dropped that label to become, at the bare minimum, a league-average quarterback, if not better. The former number one overall pick was benched early into his second season. Now, he ranks eighth in passing yards (2,197), even above players like Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes .

Now, Young's numbers were even better to start the season. His production has taken a major hit in recent weeks as he has had to withstand a beaten-up offensive line. His small stature is still a major concern for some, too. The Panthers can at least breathe a sigh of relief that they did, in fact, draft a franchise signal caller 1-1 back in 2023.

14. Jayden Daniels, Washington Commanders

Jayden Daniels has remained steady throughout his career. He was able to earn Rookie of the Year honors a couple of years ago by throwing with accuracy and not making mistakes in the air. His big plays would come in the form of runs more so than passes. That remains the case to this day. Daniels is accurate and rarely has turnover-worthy throws, but he doesn't take a lot of chances.

Luckily, he is arguably the best rushing quarterback in the league outside of Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson, the latter of whom is currently out with an injury and, therefore, not on this list. The concern with that is that injuries have plagued Daniels throughout the last two seasons. He was limited to seven games last season because of hamstring and elbow injuries. Daniels again hurt his elbow this year and was forced to miss time.

The Washington Commanders' offense has weirdly made some massive mistakes this season. Daniels is also without his top receiving target. He and his team haven't been able to put it all together since an incredible rookie season, but the potential is still there with the former Heisman winner from LSU.

Bo Nix is perhaps the hardest player on this list to rank. For three quarters, he looks like a below-average quarterback. His Denver Broncos tend to go into that fourth quarter trailing, despite how great the defense is. Then, Nix and the rest of his team pick up their play. Nix, in particular, becomes elite in crunch time and is clearly one of the most clutch players in the NFL.

The Broncos' style shouldn't be sustainable, but it has worked for two straight seasons now. The Broncos have now won a record 16 straight one-score games . Nix also has career statistics that trump his draft class peers, despite being the sixth QB taken in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft.

If the single-season record holder for collegiate completion percentage could put it all together for entire games, he'd be elite. Instead, he ranks as just above average. The good news is that Nix has started to look better in recent weeks, and at the end of the day, winning is winning, no matter how ugly it is.

C.J. Stroud is starting to look like his old self again. In 2023, the Houston Texans drafted Stroud second overall, and he gave them one of the best rookie seasons ever. During that year, he led the league in passing yards per game and touchdown-to-interception ratio, something that only Tom Brady and Joe Montana had done before him.

Fans assumed MVPs would come in the years to follow, but Stroud has been mediocre ever since, and the Texans have had to rely on dominant defense to win games. The winning stopped after that, too, as Houston started the season 0-4. The Texans have gone 3-1 since, and Stroud has found a way to move the ball down the field and score at a high level again.

Stroud has 10 touchdown passes over his last three games, most recently putting up a 384-yard, five-touchdown performance that was arguably the best of his career. The quarterback's confidence has seemingly increased ever since Houston traded for his old college buddy, Marvin Harrison Jr. Hopefully, this version of Stroud is here to stay.

The Detroit Lions' offense has remained explosive with Jared Goff leading the way. The pioneer of the fifth highest-scoring offense has been able to be aggressive without making mistakes. Goff has just two interceptions on the year. Goff was above 4,400 yards in each of the past four seasons as well.

He was a touchdown away in 2020 from being above the 30-touchdown mark in each of those years. In Los Angeles, Goff was a game-manager, despite his number one overall pick status. In Detroit, he has been truly one of the game's best quarterbacks.

10. Trevor Lawrence, Jacksonville Jaguars

Trevor Lawrence entered the NFL as the number one pick and one of the most highly touted prospects in NFL history. All he'd done as an amateur was win, but that didn't happen right away with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Lawrence was good but not great, and therefore a letdown in the eyes of many.

That isn't the case anymore. The Jaguars are clearly one of the best teams in football, and T-Law is clearly one of the best quarterbacks in the league. Lawrence has 1,932 yards for 18 touchdowns, and his 8.6 yards per attempt are the most in the NFL for QBs who have played the entire season.

Lawrence has a prototypical build, and he has used it to deliver strikes in the end zone and orchestrate a high-octane offense all season long.

Caleb Williams is fresh off a four-interception game . He also missed three weeks because of a hamstring injury, one that he caught a lot of flak for because some fans thought he reacted as though he'd suffered a season-ending injury. Even so, Williams is clearly a stud, and MVPs seem likely to be in his future.

Williams entered the NFL as one of the most highly touted prospects ever. His arm strength and ability to fit the ball into tight windows is incredible, and he regularly makes highlight plays that look like they would never be attempted outside of backyard football games.

With a young core around him and a play-calling genius in Ben Johnson as his head coach, Williams should only continue to get better. His potential is that of the best quarterback in the NFL. For now, though, he just narrowly makes the top 10.

With CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens to throw to, Dak Prescott is again putting up huge numbers. It helps that the Dallas Cowboys' offense has found more balance with Javonte Williams thriving out of the backfield, too. Prescott ranks third with 2,381 passing yards. That is exactly where he finished last year and in 2023.

The numbers are undeniable, but with a career 2-5 postseason record, Prescott needs to prove himself just a little bit more when the games matter the most.

Brock Purdy entered the NFL as Mr. Irrelevant and the low man on the totem pole of the San Francisco 49ers depth chart. When he was eventually given a chance to play, Purdy started a trend of winning a whole lot of games, and that trend hasn't stopped over the years. However, he was given the game-manager label.

At this point, there is no denying Purdy as an uber-talented player who would find success regardless of the system he is in and the personnel that he is surrounded by. Purdy's 81.4 QBR leads the entire NFL, and he has built himself a nice MVP case. The 49ers' 7-1 record is tied for the best in the NFL.

Like Purdy, Love has skyrocketed up this list ranking the starting quarterbacks across the league due to his play in 2026. First in passing yards (2,618) and third in passing touchdowns (19), the Green Bay Packers quarterback has looked like a superstar. Love just edges out Purdy here because he has shown a little more willingness to take and execute on shots down the field.

Matthew Golden and Christian Watson have been the beneficiaries, and they are starting to join conversations about being elite as well. The Packers rank 31st in rushing offense, but it hasn't mattered because Love has taken multiple steps forward.

The reigning NFL MVP, Matthew Stafford , is past his prime and now down his elite receiver duo of Davante Adams and Puka Nacua. Even so, Sean McVay and the Los Angeles Rams trust him with the football in his hands. Despite being 38 years old, Stafford ranks first in attempts (346) and completions (230).

He had a 5,000-yard season dating all the way back to 2011, and he threw for a league-leading 4,707 yards and 46 touchdowns as recently as last year. The gunslinger is a lot safer with the football than he was earlier in his career. Hopefully the Rams will finally be able to get healthy before the start of the postseason.

Drake Maye was ClutchPoints' preseason pick for MVP. He'd just finished second in MVP voting the year prior and led the New England Patriots to a Super Bowl appearance, so it was easy to predict him as the next Tom Brady in New England. Of course, though, fans were quickly reminded that the G.O.A.T. is the greatest of all time for a reason.

Maye struggled to start the season, making uncharacteristically poor throws and bad decisions. He had two losses and six interceptions through the Patriots' first three games of the season. Maye has since gotten back on track. He has 17 touchdown passes over the last six weeks and has played at an MVP level during that time.

Now, the disastrous start will likely prevent Maye from actually earning that hardware, but it is clear that he will be a very good quarterback for a very long time.

Patrick Mahomes is certainly the best player of a generation. He has three Super Bowl MVPs to his name to go along with five total appearances in the big dance. His resume is enhanced by two regular season MVPs and some of the best statistical performances ever, including a 50-touchdown season and two 5,000-yard seasons.

Last year, Mahomes suffered a knee injury that altered his future outlook, and his numbers haven't been as lofty in recent years as they were earlier on in his career. Still, Mahomes was ranked as the best quarterback coming into the year because he is a proven winner and a player that nobody should ever doubt.

Yet again, though, Mahomes has been more game manager who just does what it takes to win than a highlight-waiting-to-happen gunslinger. He is still one of the best players in the NFL, he still does some crazy things with the football in his hands, and he is still a threat to win the Super Bowl. He also just proved his toughness yet again after returning to play after suffering an elbow injury that looked nasty at first glance. For now, though, Mahomes has to be docked a couple of spots.

Josh Allen is building himself another MVP case. Of course, Allen is one of the best rushing quarterbacks ever. In fact, his 88 rushing touchdowns are by far the most ever and well over double that of a legend like Michael Vick. Allen has a rocket launcher for an arm that allows for plenty of big plays through the air, too.

The Buffalo Bills are tied for the best record in the NFL. A lot of regular seasons wins is nothing new for Allen and company. Will this be the year he finally breaks out in the playoffs?

When Joe Burrow is healthy and on the football field, he is an MVP candidate and arguably the best quarterback in the world. Unfortunately, about half of Burrow's seasons have been riddled by injuries, including last year, when he was limited to just eight games. Before that, the Cincinnati Bengals star suffered a torn ACL as a rookie that limited him to 10 games, and he again played just 10 games in 2023 because of a wrist injury.

Luckily, 2026 is one of those seasons where Burrow is staying healthy, and fans have been rewarded with video game-like numbers. The QB responsible for one of the greatest Heisman Trophy-winning seasons ever leads the NFL with 23 touchdowns, and he is second with 2,386 passing yards.

Those numbers have Burrow tied as the MVP favorite and earn the quarterback the title of the best quarterback in the NFL right now. Burrow has so much touch on his passes, and it helps that the receiver duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins is arguably the best in the league. Burrow's record-breaking streak of four straight games with four total touchdowns and a completion percentage over 70% just came to a close.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins reunion is about Vikings maximizing their roster; fellow QB Kyler Murray in line for reserve role

articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell and quarterback Kirk Cousins are separated by about 3 years of age. Before they spent two seasons together in Minnesota, they first worked with one another in Washington.

They have a history of being in lockstep. It apparently repeated itself on Tuesday.

On the day of the league's trade deadline, the 41-year-old O'Connell, now in his fifth season leading the Vikings, had been granted permission to contact the 38-year-old Cousins, who was nine starts into his 15th NFL season.

But as O'Connell was dialing Cousins, the veteran signal-caller dialed the renowned play-caller.

"I don't know how that works on the iPhone, but I think if I had to hit the green button, it was me who picked up," O'Connell said, explaining the uncanny moment.

Cousins told reporters in his Wednesday news conference that Las Vegas Raiders general manager John Spytek and head coach Klint Kubiak were essentially putting the ball in the QB's court , when it came to his then-potential trade to the Vikings.

"And I said, 'Well, let me talk to Kevin,'" Cousins said.

"Just wanted to give him a call and get on the same page, and [I] thought we had a good conversation. … Kevin knows me. Kevin knows what I do well. Kevin knows what I don't do well. Kevin knows what I can handle. Kevin knows what I can't handle. And I think that helps."

O'Connell said that, coming out of that phone conversation, he felt "really strongly" about the move the Vikings had on the table.

It got done, with the Raiders sending Cousins back to Minnesota, where the four-time Pro Bowler last played from 2018-23, and Vegas getting a 2027 third-round pick in exchange .

The Cousins trade had a ripple effect across the NFL. Not only did it stimulate plenty of conversation — even Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur offered his take on the transaction Wednesday — but it also marked the beginning of the Fernando Mendoza era in Las Vegas . This year's No. 1 overall pick had been learning under Cousins and now has the keys to the Raiders' offense.

As for Minnesota, its season-opening QB1, Kyler Murray, will take a backseat. The game of musical chairs at a position O'Connell played and then earned significant praise for developing continues, this time with a full-circle moment that's a bit surreal.

Cousins joining a Vikings team that won its first six games of the season before dropping two in a row could signify the beginning of the end of the Murray experiment in Minnesota. The Vikings inked the two-time Pro Bowler to a one-year deal this past offseason , reportedly on the veteran minimum.

Murray, a dual-threat QB whom the Arizona Cardinals selected first overall back in 2019, was named Minnesota's starter over 2024 No. 10 overall pick J.J. McCarthy. The Vikings wound up trading the still-23-year-old McCarthy to the New York Giants in late September. McCarthy's gone on to inject some hope into a 5-2-1 Giants team that lost Jaxson Dart for the year in Week 2.

Meanwhile, Murray had a difficult time finding a groove under O'Connell. Injuries disrupted him, too. Murray suffered a concussion early in the season opener . Now he's dealing with a hamstring strain that kept him out of Monday night's loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Murray remains "week-to-week" with that injury, O'Connell said Wednesday.

When asked directly if Murray will have a chance to battle for the first-string quarterback job when he's healthy again, O'Connell indicated that a midseason competition at the position isn't really feasible.

"We acquired Kirk to join a 6-2 football team and play," O'Connell noted.

O'Connell delivered the news of the Cousins deal to a quarterback room that consists of not only Murray but also veteran Carson Wentz and second-year QB Max Brosmer, both of whom played in the 23-6 defeat to the Bills.

When discussing Murray and Wentz specifically, O'Connell said they know that general manager Nolan Teasley as well as he and every other team staffer involved in the trade were "making it in the best interest of the Minnesota Vikings."

"We're trying to do everything we can to become the best version of our team this year in 2026," O'Connell said. "We have a lot of confidence in what that can be, but we also know that it's almost the middle of November. So the time is upon us where we need to be the type of team that we want to be to hopefully matter when December and January roll around."

Teasley pointed out in his appearance Wednesday: "The quarterback position is one that can impact the entire team. And, in all honesty, this roster has earned the right to explore the potential to maximize where we can take this thing."

Minnesota has a Super Bowl-caliber defense. Led by esteemed coordinator Brian Flores, the unit is allowing only 14.5 points per game, the fewest any team is giving up this season.

Conversely, the Vikings' offense is 27th in the league with 18.3 points per game. For reference, during the 2022 campaign, Cousins' lone full season with O'Connell in Minnesota, the Vikings went 13-4 and averaged 24.9 points, good for the eighth most of any team in the NFL that time around.

O'Connell didn't close the door on Murray's long-term future in Minnesota and reminded the assembled media that every player needs to be prepared because of how volatile the NFL can be. For now, though, Murray has to get healthy. Wentz, who's nursing a minor ankle injury, could be Cousins' backup in the meantime.

The goal is for Cousins to start Sunday on the road against the Packers, but neither O'Connell nor Cousins could commit to that happening on Wednesday.

If Cousins does in fact start on Sunday in Green Bay, it will be quite the scene. Lambeau Field is where he played his last game for the Vikings, an appearance that was cut short by an Achilles tear that required him to be carted off and ultimately undergo season-ending surgery amid the 2023 campaign.

The subsequent offseason, Cousins signed a massive deal with the Atlanta Falcons , and the Vikings drafted McCarthy as his replacement.

Cousins' two-season run in Atlanta didn't go according to plan. The Falcons immediately drafted Michael Penix Jr. No. 8 overall, plus Cousins dealt with more injuries, notably picking up shoulder and elbow issues before being benched 14 games into his first go-around with the team.

He was pretty effective in Vegas, however. Cousins threw 20 touchdown passes against eight picks while going 4-5 with the Raiders. Only Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow has tossed more TDs (23) in the 2026 season.

A lot's gone down since Cousins' last Vikings game at Lambeau.

"It means a lot to play at Lambeau Field no matter what the circumstances," he said Wednesday. "I think knowing that that was where I was carted off and had thoughts, 'Is this my last game and is this my last game as a Viking?' and to be back there wearing the purple and gold, it has meaning, but you have to go make it mean something with the way you play."

O'Connell said it's already been great having Cousins back in the building, adding that "you feel his energy right away."

It's clear Cousins' relationships with Vikings personnel were lasting.

He won't have to start over in that department. On the other hand, he will need a new place to live.

Cousins shared that his previous home was sold quickly when he knew his first Vikings run came to an end. His wife, Julie, is in the process of helping his family find a new spot.

"They're over across the street in the hotel with my boys, and we're figuring it out," Cousins said. "I was hoping they were going to come with me, but I said, 'What are you thinking, Julie?' It was her call. And she said, 'I don't think we can pull the boys out of school and baseball and their friends.' "She picked them up from school, and she said, 'Here's the situation. Dad got traded to the Minnesota Vikings. What would you guys want to do?' And they looked at her, and they said, 'Let's go.' So they're across the street, and they're ready and excited for the next several weeks."

"They're over across the street in the hotel with my boys, and we're figuring it out," Cousins said. "I was hoping they were going to come with me, but I said, 'What are you thinking, Julie?' It was her call. And she said, 'I don't think we can pull the boys out of school and baseball and their friends.'

"She picked them up from school, and she said, 'Here's the situation. Dad got traded to the Minnesota Vikings. What would you guys want to do?' And they looked at her, and they said, 'Let's go.' So they're across the street, and they're ready and excited for the next several weeks."

Teasley was asked if bringing on Cousins could be a solution that extends beyond this season.

"There's always potential for that, but this is really about 2026," he said, "and that's where we're focused. But we understood everything that we were inheriting. So we'll take that into account, and then when that time comes, we'll address it."

Cousins' familiarity with O'Connell and his offense will allow him to somewhat seamlessly slide back into things. Vikings quarterbacks have registered a combined 60.9% completion rate this season.

That figure hardly satisfies a completion-based scheme.

Cousins should be able to rectify that. As O'Connell explained Wednesday, where there's completions to be had, Cousins is going to find them.

"The expectation I know Kirk's going to put on himself is going to be high, and that's one of the things you love about him," O'Connell said, "but I also want to make sure that we can progressively build this thing and not ask too much of him early on, knowing that we want to be playing our best football in December.

"We want to be playing our best football in December, but also make sure that we understand the point in the season that we're at right now, we need to specifically start playing better on offense and more consistent to be the team we think we can become."

articles.title: Sunday night vs Steelers will somehow be a Burrow first
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow told reporters he loves playing in primetime, "to be able to showcase what we do and how hard we work."
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow somehow hasn't played in a primetime time at home against an AFC North opponent, ahead of an NFL Week 10 showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers on NBC's Sunday Night Football at Paycor Stadium.

Burrow was injured when the Bengals hosted the Steelers in primetime in 2020 and 2025 .

"This is why, you know, I love playing in primetime," Burrow said. "Some guys would rather play at (1:00). I'd rather play every game, Sunday night, Monday night football. I want to be able to showcase what we do and how hard we work and go and showcase what we can do to the world, and this is a big moment for it."

"I think you gotta treat every game like it's its own," Burrow continued. "I think you could say (the Bengals thrive in primetime) over the years, but that's just because, you know, those games coincided with us playing great. I'm not sure it has anything to do with the moment or the big-timeness of that game. I just think we're a good football team."

"The atmosphere (Sunday night) is gonna be great," Burrow added. "Sunday Night Football with first place in the division on the line. ... That last game against Tennessee is about as loud as I've heard (Paycor Stadium), and I've heard it pretty loud. This weekend I think will be even more amped up and ready to go."

Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers' announcement in May that he'll retire after the 2026 NFL season means the Bengals may be facing the future Pro Football Hall of Famer for the final time.

"He's one of the greatest that's ever done it, and he's 40-whatever and still doing that at a high level," Burrow said of Rodgers. "I would have trouble calling it quits when I'm still playing like that at that age, and so I've enjoyed watching him for a long time. And this year I think he's playing so well, and he really played great in the last game we played, dang near perfect, and made me feel like I had to be perfect the whole time, too, and he's done that for a long time."

Burrow, who has 16 touchdown passes over his past four games, was named one of two FedEx Air & Ground NFL Players of the Week.

During NFL Network analysis ahead of the Bengals' Week 9 win against Atlanta in Spain, Pro Football Hall of Famer Kurt Warner said he thinks Burrow, Warner's NFL MVP pick, can lead the team back to the Super Bowl.

Before the Atlanta game, Burrow greeted Spanish soccer star Ferran Torres.

After the game, Burrow said Ja'Marr Chase "was unbelievable" against the Falcons, swapped jerseys with Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, and told reporters he'd love to play in the first NFL game in Tokyo.
